Mosyle is the only solution that integrates in a single professional grade platform all the solutions necessary to seamlessly and automatically deploy, manage, and protect Apple devices at work. Over 45,000 organizations trust Mosyle to make millions of Apple devices work ready with no effort and at an affordable cost. Request your EXTENDED TRIAL today and understand why Mosyle is everything you need to work with Apple.

I’ve spent the past few weeks thinking about how Apple built up the best deal in enterprise AI. Two things happened that make me think Apple knew that all along (or maybe they didn’t and got lucky). Meta released its most capable open-weight model yet and optimized it to run on a Mac Studio. I also spent time with Osaurus, an app that runs a usable local AI model on something as small as a 16 GB Apple silicon laptop without needing a network connection. They even have two models that will run on 8 GB.

The Xserve has been dead since 2011, but its spiritual successor sits on a desk rather than in a rack.

About Apple @ Work: Bradley Chambers has been an Apple IT admin since 2009. Through his experience deploying and managing firewalls, switches, a mobile device management system, enterprise grade WiFi, 1000s of Macs, and 1000s of iPads, Bradley will highlight ways in which Apple IT managers deploy Apple devices, build networks to support them, train users, share stories from the trenches of IT management, and ways Apple could improve its products for IT departments.

For the last few years, the narrative has been that Apple fell behind in AI because it didn’t have a frontier model. Siri AI got delayed, and the Apple Intelligence rollout was not great. In hindsight, I think Apple was right not to run that race, as the frontier-model business has turned into somewhat of a capital bonfire. Every frontier lab is spending billions on GPUs to be the best for a few months at a time, and the moment a model is good enough, someone else releases an open-weight version that runs on hardware you already own.

Open-weight models prove it: Muse Spark Open has 816 billion parameters, 42 billion active parameters, and a million-token context window, and Meta is giving it away. Apple didn’t build that LLM. It built the hardware that runs it. With that being said, Siri is still far behind.

Apple built the infrastructure for everything but the frontier model

Look at what Apple has shipped while everyone was waiting on them to try to compete with Anthropic or OpenAI. With Apple silicon’s unified memory, the GPU can use up to 512 GB of memory on a single Mac Studio, instead of being limited to whatever fits on a graphics card.

MLX is Apple’s machine learning framework, and it’s built specifically for the unified memory architecture of Apple silicon. If you’ve used NumPy, the API will feel familiar right away. On top of that, MLX includes higher-level packages for neural networks and optimizers, along with function transformations for automatic differentiation and graph optimization, so you can build more complex models without giving up efficiency. It also has bindings in Swift, C++, and C, which means it runs on any Apple platform.

Apple’s own Machine Learning Research post shows four M5 Ultra Mac Studios running Muse Spark Open at over 36 tokens per second, which is faster than you can read, while peaking around 300 watts per machine.

Meta’s own words on the setup:

Apple’s unified memory architecture lets the M5 Ultra’s integrated GPU use up to 512 GB per Mac Studio, so two machines can hold an entire model. And the chip’s 1.2 TB/s of memory bandwidth is fast enough to read the small slice each token needs. The result is two Mac Studios behave like one supercomputer with a terabyte of unified memory.

We tested a range of agentic workflows running entirely on-device, using Muse Code powered by Muse Spark Open, including shipping real iOS changes to Ice Cubes (an open-source Mastodon client) — bug fixes, new features, full build — and driving DaVinci Resolve end to end, with the model reviewing footage frame by frame to find the strongest moments and crop them vertically.

That’s the Xserve pitch, rebuilt for 2026. Apple killed the Xserve in 2011 because nobody wanted a Mac in a data center. The Mac mini came along and provided some new use cases over the years. Now, a couple of Mac Studios can host a model that would otherwise require a rack of Nvidia hardware and a power budget to match, and it does so quietly enough to sit under a desk. Apple wasn’t trying to compete with OpenAI, Anthropic, or Nvidia. It was building the infrastructure for everything except the frontier model, and it looks like that’s where the market is going. A company like MacStadium has to be loving this future as well.

It works on a 16 GB MacBook too

The Mac Studio story is the headline, but what matters most to most IT teams is at the other end of the lineup. I had Terence Pae, co-founder and CEO of Osaurus, on the Apple @ Work podcast last week. Osaurus is a free, open-source AI tool for the Mac. It helps manage local models that work offline, but it can also call a frontier model when needed. A really cool feature, when it does this, is that Osaurus runs a small local model first to find names, phone numbers, and account numbers in whatever you pasted, and swaps them for placeholders before anything goes to Claude or OpenAI.

Osaurus has no servers and no customer database. If the company went out of business tomorrow, the app would keep running until macOS broke it. Individuals use it for free. Workspaces, the paid tier, is for teams who want to share agents across their own Macs. There’s a Windows beta as well, which I think helps Apple’s case more than it hurts it. When the same app runs on both platforms, the Mac’s unified memory is the difference.

Wrap up

In talking with him, Terence mentioned he wouldn’t be surprised if a local model matches what today’s frontier models can do by this time next year. I believe him, and that’s the point. The frontier will keep moving, but good enough keeps moving too, and good enough is what most employees need most of the day. Apple spent the AI race building memory, bandwidth, and a framework instead of trying to match the frontier, and the narrative was that they were behind.

Now the most capable open-weight model in the US is optimized for the Mac.

title: VSCO launches its first native Mac photo editor with RAW support, batch editing, more
snippet: VSCO today released Studio Pro Desktop, its first native photo editor for Mac, bringing many of the company’s familiar editing tools to macOS, alongside new features aimed at photographers working with large numbers of images. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
VSCO today released Studio Pro Desktop, its first native photo editor for Mac, bringing many of the company’s familiar editing tools to macOS, alongside new features aimed at photographers working with large numbers of images. Here are the details.

VSCO comes to the Mac

Professional and amateur photographers just got a new alternative for editing and managing their photos on Mac with the release of VSCO Studio Pro, a native macOS app that brings the company’s popular editing tools to the desktop for the first time.

More than that, VSCO Studio Pro integrates with the company’s broader ecosystem of photography tools, allowing users to manage their workflow from importing and editing photos to delivering finished images to clients through VSCO Galleries, without having to manually export and upload them to another app.

It also supports keyboard shortcuts similar to those found in other popular photo editors, making it easier for photographers familiar with those apps to get started.

Here’s Eric Wittman, CEO of VSCO, on today’s launch:

“Photographers deserve tools built around how they actually work. […] 75% of VSCO Pro members have used our presets in the last six months. Now those looks live on the desktop, with one connected workflow from camera to client delivery and nothing getting in the way.

The first thing users will notice, and then continue to notice when using VSCO Studio Pro, is how fast it is. From changing the grid size, to sorting images, to applying presets by rolling the cursor over each of the 200+ presets, pretty much everything about VSCO Studio Pro feels as real-time and instant as it can be when dealing with large numbers of images.

As for importing photos, VSCO Studio Pro supports Apple Photos, local folders, SD cards, and external drives, and offers RAW compatibility with more than 800 cameras from 20 brands. Users can also choose whether to work with files in their original location or copy them elsewhere.

Under the hood, VSCO Studio Pro Desktop combines Apple’s Core Image RAW processing with the company’s own Reflex image processing engine, which handles presets and editing adjustments.

Batch editing in VSCO Studio Pro Desktop can handle anywhere from two to 500 images at once, which is great for quickly applying the same preset or film-inspired look (including Kodak Portra, Kodachrome, Fujifilm Velvia, and Kodak Tri-X), or making adjustments to an entire set of photos simultaneously, with changes appearing across all selected images in real time.

And speaking of presets, VSCO Studio Pro packs an exclusive one called IOE1 Pro, developed with photographer Joe Greer. IOE1 Pro, as well as VSCO’s other presets, allow users to adjust the strength, color, tone, and contrast, further helping them fine-tune each look to their liking.

VSCO Studio Pro’s editing tools include the usual suspects photographers might expect from photo editing software, including exposure, contrast, fade, highlights, shadows, whites, blacks, skin tone, temperature, tint, hue, saturation, lightness, sharpening, clarity, vignetting, and grain adjustments for strength, size, and color.

VSCO is also working to expand its toolset to include bloom and halation effects, curves, masks, and a remove tool for users looking for more control over their edits and to make more precise, localized adjustments to their images.

Also in the works are new organizational features, including projects for managing groups of photos, as well as culling tools that will allow users to rate images with stars and mark them as accepted or rejected, making it easier to sort through large photo collections.

Once users are happy with their adjustments, they can export their photos individually or in batches, choosing the file name, format, resolution, and compression quality. VSCO Studio Pro also offers resizing presets for web, social media, and client delivery, as well as the option to save the finished images to a folder of their choice.

And speaking of client delivery, users can publish their edited photos directly to VSCO Galleries, allowing them to share full-resolution images without having to export them and upload them separately elsewhere.

title: Chrome 157 for Googlebook rolling out with 27 new features, improvements
snippet: Chrome 157 widely rolled out last week, and Google is now sharing the extensive changelog for Googlebook OS. more…
fullText:
Chrome 157 widely rolled out last week, and Google is now sharing the extensive changelog for Googlebook OS.

There are five new features for the browser in version 157:

Auto-Expand Vertical Tabs on Hover: Hovering over a collapsed vertical tab rail with a mouse or trackpad now temporarily expands it as an overlay so you can read full tab titles, switch tabs, or manage groups, and retracts when you move your cursor away. This is enabled by default and can be toggled off or on in Settings > Appearance > Tab position > “Auto expand tabs on hover” or by right-clicking the vertical tab rail.

Resizable Vertical Tab Bar: You can now manually resize the vertical tab bar to view longer page titles without truncation, and Chrome remembers your custom width across browser restarts and new windows (supported when “Auto expand tabs on hover” is turned off).

Direct URLs and Back/Forward History for Settings: Individual Chrome Settings subpages now have direct web addresses (such as chrome://settings/appearance or chrome://settings/privacy) that you can type, bookmark, or link to directly. Navigating between Settings subpages also works with Chrome’s Back and Forward buttons.

Tab Sharing Controls Bar: When sharing a browser tab in video calls (such as Google Meet), Chrome now displays a persistent control bar at the top of the window to “Stop sharing” or “Share this tab instead” from any tab.

“Save As” System File Dialog: The system “Save As” file picker is now enabled by default for explicit menu save actions (such as “Save link as…”, “Save image as…”, and “Save page as…”), letting you rename files and choose a destination folder, including Google Drive or external storage.

This is followed by 22 improvements, especially for the Bookmarks Bar, Vertical Tabs, and Address Bar. Of note is the “standard desktop text-editing menu” when right-clicking the address bar.

Bookmarks Bar Right-Click Menu: Context menus now open properly when right-clicking on the bookmarks bar or bookmark folders.

Bookmarks Bar in Fullscreen: Switching tabs in fullscreen mode while vertical tabs are enabled now keeps the bookmarks bar visible.

Bookmarks Bar During Screen Sharing: Clicking on bookmark items on the bookmarks bar now responds normally while presenting or sharing your screen in Google Meet.

Pinned Tab Hover Cards: Hovering over a pinned tab consistently displays the tab preview hover card even when a vertical scrollbar is visible.

Vertical Tabs Scrollbar Alignment: Aligned scrollbar spacing between pinned and unpinned vertical tabs to prevent visual jumping when scrolling through long tab lists.

Settings Subpages on Theme Change: Switching system appearance between light and dark mode now keeps you on your current Chrome Settings subpage instead of resetting to the main Settings menu.

Launcher “New Window” Shortcut: Right-clicking or long-pressing Chrome in the app launcher or taskbar now shows a “New Window” shortcut, including when Incognito mode is disabled by enterprise policies.

Google Slides External Monitor Selection: Restored the external monitor picker in Google Slides presentation settings for dual-screen presentations with presenter view and speaker notes.

Close Third-Party Sign-In Prompts: Clicking the close (X) button on third-party Google Sign-In prompts (such as on Reddit) now cleanly dismisses the dialog without freezing.

Partial Translate in PDFs: Selecting text inside PDFs opened in Chrome tabs now shows the Partial Translate option in the right-click menu.

Opening Downloaded PDFs: Clicking a downloaded PDF in Chrome’s download manager now opens it directly in a new browser tab instead of an external system viewer.

Media Controls During Picture-in-Picture: Opening a Picture-in-Picture video window no longer causes the media controls popup in the toolbar to close early.

Web App Installation Window: Installing a window’s only open tab as a web app now opens a New Tab Page instead of leaving an empty browser window.

Web App Back Navigation: Newly opened web app windows now start with only in-app history so the back button no longer returns to pages visited before the app was installed.

Multiple Web Apps on the Same Site: Installing one web app from a site no longer causes other web apps on that same site to appear as “Already installed” or fail to open.

Address Bar Copy Selection: Right-clicking highlighted text in the address bar now opens copy options without clearing your URL selection.

Shift+Up/Down Text Selection in Address Bar: Pressing Shift+Up or Shift+Down while typing in the address bar now extends multi-line text selection instead of selecting search suggestions.

Address Bar Right-Click Menu: Right-clicking anywhere in the address bar now displays the standard desktop text-editing menu.

Ctrl+L Full URL Selection: Pressing Ctrl+L now reveals and selects the complete web address, including URL parameters.

Address Bar Suggestions Dismissal: Clicking outside the address bar now cleanly closes the suggestions dropdown so the search box doesn’t remain stuck open.

Contextual Search Privacy Notice: Contextual search now shows a non-blocking privacy notice instead of a pop-up dialog that interrupts your workflow.

Stability fixes: Stability improvements were made across browser extensions, keyboard shortcuts, and managed browser policies.

title: Everything new in iOS 27.3 beta 2
snippet: iOS 27.3 beta 2 is here. Apple’s next iPhone software update brings a ton of changes including the redesigned Health app and much more. Below, we’re collecting the new features and changes discovered during testing. more…
fullText:
iOS 27.3 beta 2 is here. Apple’s next iPhone software update brings a ton of changes including the redesigned Health app and much more. Below, we’re collecting the new features and changes discovered during testing.

iOS 27.3 beta 2 details

The second iOS 27.3 beta is available for developer beta testers. 

To update, open Settings, tap General, then Software Update. Choose iOS 27 Developer Beta under Beta Updates.

A public beta will likely follow in the days to come.

Here’s what’s new in the new iOS 27.3 beta 2 release:

iPhone Duo can now be unlocked with facial recognition (with limitations). Details here.

iPhone Duo includes a new option to lock the phone when closing from unfolded state. The setting is added to Display & Brightness in Settings app.

Calendar app has been redesigned with new bottom-oriented controls. Details here.

macOS Full Disk Access permissions have been updated. Details here.

Apple TV app adds video podcasts section. There’s also a new vertical video feature. Details here.

Siri AI gains ability to answer health-related questions. Details here.

Apple News+ Puzzles offerings expand to Australia, French Canada, and the UK. Puzzle availability varies by region.

Siri AI can now use an entire webpage in Safari for context. This works with content that isn’t in view as well.

Siri AI comes to Apple TV 4K (second- and third-gen) in tvOS 27.3 beta 2

Prior to iOS 27.3 beta 2, these changes were included:

Redesigned Health app returns in beta. It was previously previewed in iOS 27.2 beta for a few cycles. Apple signals that it will ship with iOS 27.3 before the end of this year. Details here.

Audio Intelligence features for Apple Watch, including Siri Recap and Live Rewind, are available to beta test in watchOS 27.3 beta with iOS 27.3 beta. Details here.

Apple Fitness+ adds Gym Strength workouts. Details here. 

Safari gains vertical tabs, adaptive dark mode, and more. Details here.

Siri AI language support expands to include Traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish, and Norwegian.

iPhone Duo adds Reachability accessibility feature. Originally designed to shift content down the screen on tall displays, iPhone Duo’s version is designed to shift content from the left or right across the display for reaching across wide screens.

iPadOS 27.3 adds support for Siri Mode in the Camera app, plus Visual Intelligence with Apple Pencil support.

StandBy mode on standard iPhone models has been updated to work more like iPhone Duo. For example, digital and analog clock faces are more customizable with options to set up multiple configurations of the same faces with the ability to swipe between options. These are also configurable with various colors and complications, similar to Apple Watch faces.

Siri AI is now able to take actions in apps like Calendar, Journal, Messages, Music, and more. You can ask Siri AI what it can do in supported apps to discover new capabilities. Details here.

Apple Music app splash screen highlights improved Auto Mix, reimagined Artist Pages, and Concerts For you based on listening.

We’ll keep adding discoveries as we spend more time with the update. Have you found a change in iOS 27.3 beta 2? Share it in the comments or email tips@9to5mac.com.

title: Someone rebuilt old Android versions in your browser, and it’s an instant nostalgia hit [Gallery]
snippet: The “Android Time Machine” is a fun project that puts Android versions into your browser, giving you a quick and easy chance to play around with older versions for a quick hit of nostalgia. more…
fullText:
The “Android Time Machine” is a fun project that puts Android versions into your browser, giving you a quick and easy chance to play around with older versions for a quick hit of nostalgia.

Built on the back of AOSP builds for classic Nexus devices, “Android Time Machine” lets you quickly  access older Android versions. Specifically, Android 2.1 Eclair through Android 7.1.2 Nougat. 

The simulator runs within the shell of a matching Nexus smartphone on a desktop browser, or to fit your actual smartphone if you run it on Android. 

Versions and simulated smartphones include:

	

Android 2.1 Eclair: Nexus One

Android 2.3.6 Gingerbread: Nexus S

Android 4.0.4 Ice Cream Sandwich: Galaxy Nexus

Android 4.3 Jelly Bean: Nexus 4

Android 4.4.4 KitKat: Nexus 5

Android 5.1.1 Lollipop: Nexus 6

Android 6.0.1 Marshmallow: Nexus 5X

Android 7.1.2 Nougat: Nexus 6P

The best part here is how it works on your actual smartphone. When launched in fullscreen, it  scales to match your phone’s screen – meaning it fits even devices like the Galaxy Z Fold 8’s smaller outer display (it just shows the desktop version when open). 

Since this is running through the browser and not an actual Android build, you won’t get a perfect replication. Performance is a little hit or miss, especially with certain animations, but it works really well overall. 

The browser even simulates results from each era (oh, to go back to when Google Search wasn’t an absolute mess). Similarly, Google apps and the camera are filled with placeholders since the web app can’t access the actual camera or connect to the internet to sign into a Google account.

Seeing things like the boot animations and live wallpapers from classic Nexus phones, as well as peeking back at lost apps like Google+ and Play Music, is just such a fun little piece of nostalgia. 

“Android Time Machine” is free, and the source code is available on GitHub.

title: Google launches Intelligent Eyewear glasses: $395+, pre-order today, ships Dec. 10
snippet: After years of development, Google is launching its second foray into smart glasses with Intelligent Eyewear that supports Android and iOS. Pre-orders start today at Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, with the audio glasses shipping on December 10. more…
fullText:
After years of development, Google is launching its second foray into smart glasses with Intelligent Eyewear that supports Android and iOS. Pre-orders start today at Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, with the audio glasses shipping on December 10.

Hands-on: Google and Samsung’s vision for Android XR glasses is 20/20

Intelligent Eyewear is meant to be worn all day rather than the sunglasses-heavy approach taken by others. The frames are 40-44 grams with the weight balanced evenly. 

There is a 12-megapixel ultra-wide camera for photos and videos (3K 30FPS or 1080p). You get image stabilization and HDR processing, while four microphones work to provide spatial audio capture. Google is also quite proud of its noise cancellation work.

	

There are two open-ear speakers for balanced audio and clear vocals. Control is done by a touchpad that accepts taps and swipes, or via voice commands, with Google debuting a new “Hey Gemini” hotword. 

Another way to control Intelligent Eyewear is through your Pixel Watch or Galaxy Watch, with Fitbit Air support coming next year:

Double pinch = “tap” gesture on touchpad to play/pause

Wrist turn = “swipe back” to close an experience

Palm-up double pinch = “tap and hold” to invoke Gemini (Pixel Watch only)

Each pair features a physical on/off switch so you can “wear them as regular glasses only.” On the privacy front, there is a white indicator light when you take a photo or video that gets saved to your gallery. If the light is covered or maliciously disabled, the glasses will stop recording, with Google running a hardware check when they are charging. Recording also stops when you take off the glasses.

Notably, Gemini commands that invoke the camera — like visual search or translation — will not save images or videos to your Gemini History. These visuals won’t be used to train AI models or for ad targeting. Additionally, the glasses will “automatically redact bystanders’ faces from these visuals before Gemini processes them.” 

Battery life (245mAh) is rated at nine hours on a single charge, with a fully topped-up charging case (Gentle Monster’s shown below) offering seven full charges. Power is transferred via contact pins located on the underside of the nose bridge. 

Android XR runs on the Qualcomm Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 with 2GB of RAM and 64GB of storage. Other specifications include Bluetooth 5.4, Wi-Fi 6E, and IPX4 water resistance. Samsung is responsible for engineering the hardware, while there are two eyewear brands at launch.

Warby Parker Intelligent Eyewear is available in three styles and a total of 14 variations. Alden, Reid, and Wren are inspired by the brand’s “most beloved silhouettes.” Pricing starts at $395 for optical and sun styles in Pine, Saddle, and Jet Black.

The Gentle Monster Intelligent Eyewear collection features six frames in bold colors like dark red, pink, gray, and yellow, with 16 total variations. They can be paired with tinted, clear, blue, or brown lenses, with prescription options available for most designs. Pricing starts at $449 and will be available in the US and South Korea.

Intelligent Eyewear can be used for contextual visual searches, asking Gemini about your day, and having it accomplish tasks.

“…learn the story behind a street art mural you are passing by, ask for a tailored recommendation from a ‘New Arrivals’ bookshelf, or look at an event poster to check your Calendar availability on the spot.”

“…you can add items to your grocery list with a glance or check on your Uber’s status.”

“…use your glasses to catch up on your missed group chats, respond to messages, and take phone calls hands-free.”

Google Maps offers turn-by-turn directions, while there’s real-time Google Translate in over 70 languages.

Like on phones, Gemini Guided Vision “offers conversational audio descriptions to people with vision impairments.” This can be used to read fine print, identify color differences, find items, and explore unfamiliar places.

These glasses also serve as always-available headphones with support for YouTube Music, Spotify, Apple Music, and Audible. The Glasses companion app supports:

Pixel 7 and newer

Galaxy S, Galaxy S FE, Galaxy Z Fold, Flip, and Fold Ultra series running One UI 9.0 or higher

iPhone 13 Pro and up

Pre-orders for Gentle Monster and Warby Parker Intelligent Eyewear start today with retail availability on December 10.

title: Google Wallet may soon be able to store your Social Security card

fullText:

title: China dominates battery graphite, but this startup could break the monopoly
snippet: Chinese companies maintain near total dominance of the graphite industry, but Molten Industries says its new factory in Oakland could spell the end of the monopoly.
fullText:
Electric vehicle sales in the U.S. may have leveled off, but the market for batteries inside them isn’t slowing down, quintupling in the last five years. Many of those are made in the U.S., but they’re largely dependent on China for key ingredients, including graphite.

Graphite is a key ingredient in lithium-ion batteries, where it forms the anode, the part that stores the battery’s charge. Chinese companies control about three-quarters of the graphite anode supply chain and 97% of synthetic (human-made) graphite anode production, according to Benchmark Mineral Intelligence. One five-year-old startup, Molten Industries, is working to break that dominance.

Molten Industries has started operating a demonstration plant in Oakland meant to prove the technology works, the company exclusively told TechCrunch. The plant is will pave the way for U.S.-made graphite to win a share of the market.

“The new plant will be producing graphite that’s at cost parity with China plus tariffs,” Caleb Boyd, co-founder and CTO of Molten Industries, told TechCrunch. In other words, once U.S. import taxes are added to Chinese graphite, Molten’s price would match it. He said future plants should match China’s cost even without tariffs, which he called a built-in advantage of the technology.

Molten’s Oakland plant will make about 300 metric tons of graphite annually, which is enough for 300 megawatt-hours of batteries. That’s enough for about 4,300 EVs. The bulk of the output will go to undisclosed customers that are testing it in their battery cells.

The next facility, which Molten has yet to announce, will take the same template used in the Oakland plant and replicate it several times over, said Boyd.

The startup’s technology began in a Silicon Valley garage. It uses electrical resistive heating, which passes electricity through a material to heat it, to split methane (the main ingredient in natural gas) into pure carbon and hydrogen. “You can think of it almost like a massive toaster,” Boyd said. The company says the system uses three times less electricity than existing methods, and it runs on natural gas, which is cheap and plentiful in the U.S.

“We think it’s very hard to compete with China if you’re just copying their processes and trying to compete on cost,” said Kevin Bush, who co-founded Molten Industries with Boyd and is the company’s CEO. “So we are using a resource in the United States that’s abundant in natural gas, and we’ve brought some innovation to actually be able to drive down the cost of graphite production globally.”

Here’s how the chemistry works: When methane (CH4) is heated without oxygen, each molecule breaks into one carbon atom and four hydrogen atoms. The hydrogen atoms pair up into hydrogen gas (H2), which Molten sells at market prices to a customer next door. The carbon is then processed to meet battery makers’ requirements.

The basic idea of using heat to separate methane has been around for over a century, but early attempts to commercialize it ran into trouble. Carbon built up and clogged the reactor, and Boyd said no company before Molten had been able to produce high-quality graphite this way.

Solving that problem changed the company’s direction. Boyd and Bush — both materials science PhDs from Stanford — originally set out to make clean hydrogen from natural gas. Most hydrogen today comes from steam reforming, a cheap but polluting process. The two wanted to reap the benefits of a low-cost feedstock like natural gas without the pollution, and they expected to sell the leftover carbon as a by-product.

But as they experimented with ways to keep the reactor clean, “we actually started making this really high-quality graphite,” Boyd said, which “changed the entire economics of what we were doing.” Molten went from a hydrogen company that happened to sell graphite to a battery-grade graphite company that happens to sell hydrogen.

The company says both businesses could bring in billions of dollars. If Molten supplied the entire U.S. battery market, it could also provide about a third of the hydrogen used in the country, the company claims. Other uses for high-quality graphite, like thermal batteries that store energy as heat, could expand both markets further.

The new factory, Boyd said, “is really a milestone, not just for the company, we think, but globally.”

fullText:
Google today announced Android XR audio glasses called Intelligent Eyewear that notably support iOS with Made for iPhone certification.

Hands-on: Google and Samsung’s vision for Android XR glasses is 20/20

Intelligent Eyewear is made by Samsung with frame designs from Gentle Monster and Warby Parker. There are 30 unique designs in total, and the frames weigh 40-44 grams with a 12-megapixel ultra-wide camera. 

Google’s Glasses companion client for iOS handles compute, including HDR processing, and saves images and videos (up to 90 seconds) to Apple Photos. The Made for iPhone certification comes into play for Wi-Fi Aware connectivity that allows for fast media transfers.  

	

On the privacy front, there is a blinking white indicator light when you use the camera to take pictures or record clips that are saved to your library. If the light is covered or disabled, the glasses will stop recording, with Android XR running a hardware check when charging.

Warby Parker

Gemini commands that use the camera, like visual search or translation, don’t trigger the light because those photos or videos are not saved anywhere, including Gemini History. Before that media reaches the cloud, Google redacts faces from video feeds and filters out bystander voices. This processing is done by the companion app. Additionally, that media isn’t used to train AI models or target ads. 

Other key specifications include four microphones and two open-ear speakers. Besides voice commands with the “Hey Gemini” hotword, there is a touchpad that accepts taps and swipes. A physical on/off switch lets you wear Intelligent Eyewear as regular glasses. 

On iOS, Gemini can make calls, send 1:1 messages (including via iMessage), and receive notifications.

Gentle Monster

Battery life is rated at nine hours on a single charge, while there’s a charging case that stores seven charges. Features include turn-by-turn Google Maps directions and real-time translation. On the streaming front, there’s support for Apple Music, Spotify, YouTube Music, and Audible. 

Google’s Android XR glasses require an iPhone 13 Pro or newer.

title: Nvidia says it doesn’t plan to reappoint Jensen Huang as CEO
snippet: The former CEO offered to return to his top role at the company after his resignation last week.
fullText:
Despite Nvidia founder and former CEO Jensen Huang’s recent offer to return to the chip company he helped build from the ground up, the company is not looking to take him back.

During the company’s earnings call on Tuesday, Nvidia chairman Harvey C. Jones told listeners that Huang’s return was not something that company leadership was considering.  

“On November 12, our board of directors announced that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms,” Jones said, “Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as president, CEO, and board member. The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.”

On Tuesday, Huang had posted on X that since he left the company, he has “seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” and added that “if the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”

Huang resigned last week in dramatic fashion following revelations of a number of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman who has been accused of being a Chinese intelligence agent. That woman, former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, has maintained close ties to the former Nvidia CEO for years. Critics worry that the relationship may have influenced Nvidia’s dealings with China, and U.S. intelligence officials have expressed suspicions that she works for China’s Ministry of State Security.

The development has sent shockwaves throughout the tech industry at a moment when the future of the AI business, in which Nvidia plays a pivotal role, hangs in the balance. It has also spurred investigations, including an independent investigation into Huang’s activities by Nvidia’s board and an SEC probe into Nvidia. Huang has been replaced by interim CEO Colette Kress, who is also the chipmaker’s chief financial officer and executive vice president, while the board searches for a permanent replacement. Jones added Tuesday that the company was looking at both internal and external candidates.

title: The new Apple TV has twice as much RAM as the previous model, but apps and games can’t use it
snippet: The new Apple TV 4K features an A19 chip inside with 128 GB storage and 8 GB RAM, twice the amount of memory as the previous version. Presumably, the supply crunch surrounding the memory chips is part of the reason this generation of Apple TV box jumped to a $299 price point as well. However, although the specs have been upgraded, apps and games are not actually able to use more RAM for themselves. Apps on Apple TV are limited by the operating system to 2 GB RAM each, and that cap has not changed on the fourth-generation box. more…
fullText:
The new Apple TV 4K features an A19 chip inside with 128 GB storage and 8 GB RAM, twice the amount of memory as the previous version. Presumably, the supply crunch surrounding the memory chips is part of the reason this generation of Apple TV box jumped to a $299 price point as well.

However, although the specs have been upgraded, apps and games are not actually able to use more RAM for themselves. Apps on Apple TV are limited by the operating system to 2 GB RAM each, and that cap has not changed on the fourth-generation box.

Obviously, most of the apps you run on Apple TV are streaming service clients, which generally have much smaller RAM requirements anyway. However, ostensibly, Apple markets the Apple TV as a gaming device and RAM constraints matter much more there. 

A hypothetically graphics-intensive game will easily hit the 2 GB RAM ceiling, and some fans had hoped that the new box with the new chip and double the internal memory would help here. Unfortunately, with the current tvOS software, that is not the case. 

9to5Mac independently confirmed that an Apple TV app is force-quit by the system when it allocates more than two gigabytes of memory for its process. The developer API os_proc_available_memory function also reports a 2 GB limit to the app, the same value as the third-gen Apple TV.

It is unclear whether this is an intentional policy decision, or an oversight. Nevertheless, the 2 GB limit is the status quo. Tangentially, it’s worth noting that the 128 GB of onboard storage is also not usable by a single app or game; tvOS imposes app bundle limits of about 4 gigabytes with apps able to reserve about 20 GB extra for some assets. 

Regarding the unchanged RAM limit despite doubling the internal memory on the chip, there is some speculation that Apple opted to reserve a portion of the system memory to help the performance of the Siri AI models. However, this doesn’t make too much sense to us. The most complex Siri AI features you can do on the TV offload to a connected iPhone or server backend anyway. The same Siri AI features are also available on the prior two generations of Apple TV hardware, so it doesn’t seem like RAM constraints are a meaningful factor. 

One group of users hoping for more RAM in the Apple TV was the game decomp community, which use AI to get AAA studio games running on anything from an Apple TV to an iPhone. Some of their projects have run into the 2GB tvOS limit previously, and were hoping that the new Apple TV would alleviate that. So far, that is simply not the case.

title: Samsung supplier leak suggests mystery ‘bezel-less’ Galaxy 27 display
snippet: There are rumors of a Samsung phone with an “extremely bezel-less” display coming from one of the company’s suppliers, and it might be on one of the next Galaxy S27 models. more…
fullText:
There are rumors of a Samsung phone with an “extremely bezel-less” display coming from one of the company’s suppliers, and it might be on one of the next Galaxy S27 models.

The information comes from a related supplier for Samsung and was brought up by a known leaker, Lanzuk. Their Naver post specifically mentions an “extremely bezel-less” display. What that means is up for debate, and machine translation does not clarify the original post in Korean.

The big takeaway might be that Samsung is looking to launch one of these bezel-less display options within the Galaxy S27 lineup. An early adoption might indicate that even though this supplier planned on developing these displays for an upcoming Galaxy device, Samsung may want to push the timeline forward and fit it to one of the Galaxy S27 series phones.

Which device would debut a new “extremely bezel-less” display is up in the air. Odds are it would be the most expensive option’s display that gets updated – the Galaxy S27 Ultra. It’s also possible it could show up on both the Pro and Ultra variants, to stretch the premium tag across the upper end of the lineup.

	

This leak is probably best taken with a grain of salt. The author seems to have doubts, and this seems like a 50/50 shot. But even if Samsung doesn’t shave the bezels off of one of the Galaxy S27 models, this leak still indicates a future device will get a similar display.

That previously planned iteration may even be a better version than anything the Galaxy S27 series could have. More than a proof-of-concept.

The Galaxy S27 series is expected to launch early next year. In the meantime, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is nearly bezel-less, folds, and is marked down at its best price for the holidays.

snippet: Apple will soon be adding a video podcasts section to Apple TV, which will also be available in the Apple TV app on other devices like smart TVs. fullText:
Apple will soon be adding a video podcasts section to Apple TV, which will also be available in the Apple TV app on other devices like smart TVs. That means it will come to more than a billion devices in total.

Access to the video podcasts will be free, with no requirement for an Apple TV subscription. Testing begins today, with the full rollout promised “soon” …

Apple shared the news with The New York Times.

On Monday, Apple will add a video podcasts section to Apple TV, initially just for testing with developers. They will soon be free to all users […] Apple also plans to increase the number of video podcasts on its regular Podcasts app.

The company says the move will benefit creators and listeners alike.

“We want podcasts to be available wherever people want to enjoy them — the small screens, big screens,” said Oliver Schusser, a vice president at Apple who oversees services including podcasts, television and music. “It’s really about discovery and helping the creators to reach a new audience. We didn’t approach this in a way that would financially benefit us.”

While podcasts began as audio only, it’s become increasingly common in recent years for them to be released as video also. This expands the reach to video platforms like YouTube, Hulu, and Netflix. Creators have welcomed Apple’s latest move, even if some are a little sad about what it says about the medium.

“It’s so helpful that people can go on their phones, they see a clip on Instagram, TikTok or Twitter and open the Apple app and now watch it on video,” he said. “People are already on their iPhones and they’re used to watching videos on their phones so it was the next logical step” […]

“Everything is TV now, which is a little bit heartbreaking for a lifelong audio person to say,” Ms. Martin of NPR said.

No date has yet been announced for the public rollout.

title: Nvidia promises that revenue will keep soaring — for now
snippet: Despite the turmoil Nvidia is in after the departure of its disgraced founder and CEO Jensen Huang, the company projected that its streak of record-breaking revenue isn't about to stop.
fullText:
Despite the turmoil at Nvidia following the departure of its disgraced founder and CEO Jensen Huang, the company — as expected — delivered a solid quarter on Tuesday. More importantly, Nvidia reassured investors that its streak of record-breaking revenue won’t stop.

On Tuesday, CFO-turned-interim CEO Colette Kress reported revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from the year-ago quarter and a beat above the company’s guidance. Nvidia had told Wall Street to expect $108 billion in revenue for its third quarter of fiscal 2027. Kress also projected an even bigger fourth quarter, with revenue expected to reach $130 billion, plus or minus 3%.

She also said full-year revenue is on track to exceed expectations.

“We are raising our fiscal year 2028 outlook. We expect revenue to grow approximately 75% year over year, up from 70% and off what is now a higher fiscal 2027 base,” Kress said on the quarterly conference call on Tuesday. “Our outlook considers data center readiness, the strength and durability of end customer demand, and our customers’ access to capital.”

The company also reminded investors that it was using some of its billions in cash to buy back shares. In September 2026, Nvidia increased its share buyback program by $150 billion. It spent $28.1 billion on its own shares during the quarter and still had another $227.3 billion remaining in the kitty for additional repurchases.

Ironically, Nvidia could also benefit from the plunge in its share price following Huang’s resignation last week, should shares remain depressed over the longer term. The stock is down about 10% since his departure. Investors, however, celebrated Tuesday’s quarterly results, sending shares up about 4% in after-hours trading.

Kress stressed that the company was in good shape now and for the foreseeable future, even without Huang at the helm.

“We have the best technologists on the planet with a world-class multi-year roadmap,” Kress stressed. “From a business perspective, it’s business as usual. We’ve engaged with our customers, we’ve engaged with our suppliers, our partners. They’re all 100% behind us.”

She added that the company has secured memory and advanced packaging capacity and is working with its chip manufacturer, TSMC, to “narrow the supply and demand gaps.”

title: iPhone Duo is getting three new features in iOS 27.3
snippet: iOS 27.3 launches next month and includes several exciting changes for iPhone Duo, here’s what’s new for Apple’s foldable model. more…
fullText:
iOS 27.3 launches next month and includes several exciting changes for iPhone Duo, here’s what’s new for Apple’s foldable model.

#1: Face unlock

Apple is granting iPhone Duo users one of their biggest feature requests: face unlock is coming with iOS 27.3.

Face unlock isn’t a full-fledged Face ID, and it doesn’t work for features like Apple Pay, but it is a convenient new option for unlocking your iPhone Duo just by looking at it. Per Apple: 

Use the front camera, along with a recent Touch ID or passcode authentication, to quickly unlock iPhone Duo when it’s closed. Face recognition data never leaves your device.

If your iPhone Duo has gone unused for 45 minutes or more, face unlock won’t work and you’ll need to authenticate with Touch ID or your passcode. But for most users, that probably just means using Touch ID first thing in the morning, then relying on face unlock the rest of the day.

On a related note, you can also enable Attention Aware features in iOS 27.3. These are available whether you use the face unlock feature or not, but are limited to the outer display. Once enabled, they can automatically lower the volume of alarms and timers, keep the display from dimming, and more.

Read more: iOS 27.3 adds new face unlock feature for iPhone Duo

#2: Reachability

Reachability is available on other iPhone models to move onscreen content down vertically, closer to your thumb. But on iPhone Duo with iOS 27.3, Apple has a unique twist on the feature.

Instead of helping you reach content vertically, Reachability on iPhone Duo works horizontally.

If you’re using the outer screen and find that buttons or other UI elements are out of reach, you can swipe from the side to have onscreen content shift closer to your thumb.

You can always disable Reachability if you find yourself accidentally triggering it too often. But if one-handed iPhone Duo use gives you trouble, Reachability is a great new option to have.

Read more: iOS 27.3 introduces new iPhone Duo feature for one-handed use

#3: Automatically lock when closed

What should happen when you close your iPhone Duo’s folding screen? Apple has found that users have different preferences. Some want the iPhone to stay unlocked for continued use, while others prefer that it automatically locks when closed.

In iOS 27.3, Apple adds a new setting so users can enable whichever behavior they prefer.

By default, iPhone Duo will work as it always has, staying unlocked after being closed. But inside Settings ⇾ Display & Brightness, iOS 27.3 provides the option of automatically locking upon being closed instead. You could achieve something similar before with Shortcuts, but now there’s a built-in setting too.

Bonus: Keyboard updates

It’s not exactly a “new feature,” but iPhone Duo users will also find that the system keyboard has changed in iOS 27.3. Apple tweaked the outer display keyboard to push keys closer together and make one-handed use easier.

title: iPhone 18, iPhone Air 2 get new release timing updates
snippet: Apple only launched high-end ‘Pro’ and ‘Duo’ iPhones this fall, marking a departure from previous years when more affordable models debuted too. But iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 are still coming, and a new report offers an update on release timing. more…
fullText:
Apple only launched high-end ‘Pro’ and ‘Duo’ iPhones this fall, marking a departure from previous years when more affordable models debuted too. But iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 are still coming, and a new report offers an update on release timing.

iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 suppliers planning for March launch, per report

A new report from Kim Yeong-ho at ETNews provides a fresh update on timing for the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2.

Rumors have indicated for well over a year that Apple planned to push these models out of the typical fall launch window and introduce them in early 2027 instead.

Per ETNews, Samsung and LG are providing the display panels for the new models, with Samsung the sole supplier for iPhone Air 2 and both companies splitting orders for iPhone 18. And their mass production plans signal a March release for the products.

Kim Yeong-ho, writing at ETNews:

Samsung Display plans to begin mass production in January, while LG Display will start late this year…The Korean panel makers appear to be aligning their production plans with an expected March launch.

A March launch window lines up well with when Apple tends to ramp up product introductions following a slower winter. Earlier this year, iPhone 17e debuted in March alongside new Macs and the iPad Air.

The year before, however, the iPhone 16e arrived in February instead.

With Apple shaking up its normal iPhone rollout schedule, it was anyone’s guess how soon the new models would debut. But a March launch makes sense and gives Apple a trio of new iPhones every six months—three unveiled in September, and another three in March.

title: The Android camera app that doesn’t overprocess adds new color grading sets, expands to iPhone
snippet: VWFNDR + MBL, an Android camera app that doesn’t overprocess and delivers high-quality DNG (RAW) files, is getting a 2.0 release with improved color grading and an expansion to the iPhone. more…
fullText:
VWFNDR + MBL, an Android camera app that doesn’t overprocess and delivers high-quality DNG (RAW) files, is getting a 2.0 release with improved color grading and an expansion to the iPhone.

VWFNDR + MBL launched on Android in May 2026 with a few points that stood out. A unique UI that adapts to the shot, minimal processing for a natural look, and support for DNG files at a level that only Google’s Pixel Camera app can truly compete with. 

The app has been downloaded over 300,000 times since then, and is now getting a pretty substantial update.

On Android, this comes in the form of new color grading profiles built into the app. “NATURAL,” “NIHON,” or “B+W.” The app still saves an unprocessed DNG alongside the JPG and the grading adapts across the frame rather than having a fixed result, keeping highlights and shadows in place.

	

VWFNDR explains:

Colour grades: MBL still records unprocessed Bayer RAW DNG, and the JPG it renders alongside now uses one of three grades: NATURAL, NIHON, or B+W. Grading happens on VWFNDR’s own spatial engine. Instead of applying a fixed LUT, it adapts across the frame, much like a raw editor, so highlights and shadows keep their detail. The DNG stays untouched.

Here’s what the output looks like:

B+W
NIHON
NATURAL

The rest of VWFNDR + MBL 2.0 takes place off of Android.

In a rare case of the tables turning, MBL was released first on Android, and only on Android for the first several months. But VWFNDR is now bringing the app to iPhone with support for variable aperture on iPhone 18 Pro and Content Credentials, Apple’s version of the C2PA standard that’s meant to prove a photo is real and not AI-generated.

title: Waymo suspends freeway rides nationwide after California DMV order
snippet: The DMV said Waymo's freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety. Restrictions will remain in place until Waymo can demonstrate that it has taken "effective corrective actions" to address the deficiencies.
fullText:
Waymo robotaxis are no longer allowed to operate on California freeways after the state’s Department of Motor Vehicles restricted the Alphabet-owned company’s operations following several incidents that raised safety concerns.

California’s DMV, which regulates the testing and deployment of autonomous vehicles in the state, issued the operational restrictions on Waymo on November 11. However, the restrictions weren’t made public until Tuesday. San Francisco Business Times was the first to report the order.

The DMV confirmed the new restrictions to TechCrunch, stating that the department took action after three Waymo autonomous vehicles entered an active construction closure on U.S. Route 101 near Burlingame, and another separate incident involving California Highway Patrol vehicles on Highway 280 in San Francisco.

Waymo has complied and is preventing its robotaxis from accessing freeways in any of the markets it operates in, including those outside of California. Waymo currently has commercial operations in 15 U.S. cities.

The DMV said Waymo’s freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety.

“The Department determined that Waymo’s driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present, despite a prior restriction and corrective actions implemented following similar incidents that occurred on May 18, 2026,” according to an emailed statement sent to TechCrunch.  

 The DMV said the restrictions will remain in place until Waymo can demonstrate that it has taken “effective corrective actions” to address the deficiencies. 

Waymo spokesperson Dana Gallagher told TechCrunch the company has temporarily restricted freeway operations across its other operating markets to evaluate its performance. 

“Safety is at the foundation of everything we do,” Gallagher said in a statement. “Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state. In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week. We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations.”

Waymo began offering freeway rides in late 2025, a commercial milestone that has been central to its expansion in major metro areas. Freeway access allows Waymo to connect riders to airports and other destinations more efficiently, slashing travel times by avoiding slower surface streets.

That has been particularly important in the San Francisco Bay Area because Waymo’s service area stretches from the city south to Silicon Valley. Freeway access has dramatically shortened trips across the Peninsula that previously took 45 minutes or more than an hour.

In May, Waymo abruptly stopped operating on highways. The company didn’t cite a specific reason at the time, but several social media posts showed Waymo robotaxis driving through traffic cones and struggling to navigate construction zones. 

Waymo robotaxis returned to freeways in July after the company said it updated the self-driving software system to improve performance around freeway construction zones.

title: CNET Survey: $75 Billion in Holiday Packages Could Be Vulnerable to Lurking Porch Pirates
snippet: The average package value nears $300, yet 20% of US adults don’t use security devices to help protect their deliveries due to costs.
fullText:
Imagine patiently waiting for the special-edition Legend of Zelda Nintendo Switch 2 console or the new iPhone Duo to be delivered to your door — only for it to disappear seconds after arrival. That’s the risky reality we’re facing this holiday season because of porch pirates. 

Online holiday shopping has become the go-to way for many US adults to conveniently find, compare and buy must-have gifts. But leaving those pricey gifts at your door gives thieves a better chance of snagging them in seconds if you don’t have a plan to store them out of sight.

CNET’s annual package theft survey polls US adults about their experiences with porch pirates and how they try to prevent it. This year, the average package value is close to $300, and 28% of US adults have had a package stolen, know someone who has or caught an attempted theft within the past year. Yet 20% of US adults don’t use security devices due to hardware costs or monthly subscription fees. 

			

More from CNET

But leaving your packages unguarded could be a big risk — especially during the holidays. On the other hand, bad actors have been caught in the act on home security cameras. Is it really enough to deter bad actors, and what more can you do to protect your deliveries?

CNET’s 2026 porch theft key findings 

 US adults expect an average of $276.24 in holiday package values to be delivered this season. That’s $23.82 less than CNET’s porch theft findings last year, which estimated an average of $300.06.

Over one in four (28%) have had a package taken from their porch within the past year, caught an attempted theft or know someone who has. 

With holiday shopping in full swing, 11% of US adults have had a package stolen within the past year. 

One in five (20%) don’t use security cameras due to hardware and subscription costs.

Among victims of package theft in the past year, nearly half (46%) lost tech products or accessories.

Most adults haven’t experienced package theft — yet 

CNET’s findings show that some US adults have dealt with porch theft firsthand: 8% had packages meant for themselves or their households stolen within the past year, and 5% had a delivered gift stolen. Very few (1%) caught a theft in the act on a video doorbell or security camera. 

Meanwhile, many US adults know someone who fell victim to package theft — 13% know a neighbor or community member who had a package stolen within the past year, and 12% know someone who doesn’t live in their community who has.

“Close to a third of our respondents are personally acquainted with package theft, which is still a high number compared to other issues like break-ins,” said CNET’s senior home security editor, Tyler Lacoma. “Thieves generally look for crimes of opportunity, and few things are easier than a package left on a doorstep, especially if nobody is home.”

Surprisingly, most US adults (72%) haven’t experienced package theft or know anyone who has.  

Even though the percentages above may seem low, Lacoma said that package theft typically increases during the holidays when thieves know more deliveries are likely, and new porch theft tactics are always on the horizon. 

There are reports of thieves trying Wi-Fi jamming to disable live security camera footage while they steal packages. And findings show that some are installing spy cams in high-value neighborhoods to learn your home’s layout and habits to take your packages shortly after they’re delivered. In recent years, pirates have even tracked shipping labels for high-value tech, like iPhones, to steal the package within minutes of arrival. 

So while the majority of US adults haven’t fallen victim, that shouldn’t be a sign to shrug off the concern or relax your home security measures. Instead, now’s the time to plan how to safely store your packages if they’re delivered while you’re away.

The average holiday package delivery value is $276.24

Online shopping and deliveries to your door can be a convenient way to check off holiday wish lists, but the average package value this holiday season is less than last year. CNET found that US adults plan to have an average of $276.24 in holiday packages delivered during this holiday season. That’s $23.82 less than last year’s average of $300.06. 

By generation, Millennials also have a lower estimated average package value than last year, with an average of $227.25, compared to their 2025 package value of $307.47 — an $80.22 difference, while Gen Z’s package value is only about $7 less than last year. But any package’s value is still worth taking precautions to help prevent it from being stolen.

Cole Kan / CNET

Lacoma has thoughts on why that might be. In short, lower spending could mean fewer packages. 

“I wonder if people have also simply gotten fewer packages in general this year due to tariffs, inflation and tech prices. That could pull these numbers down,” said Lacoma. But there’s a high chance that could be the case considering CNET’s 2026 annual holiday survey, which found that US adult tech spending is down to $808 — which is $123 less than last year’s average of $931. 

What are porch pirates stealing?

Thieves may not always know what’s in boxes they’re stealing but they’re willing to take a chance. We asked US adults which items were stolen in package thefts in the past year to give you a sense of what’s at risk. 

Among the items stolen, apparel and accessories were the most common goods stolen (40%). That’s followed by toys and games (23%). Then there are everyday home basics, like decor, cookware and small appliances (19%). 

But personal tech devices and accessories are still among the items stolen. Small accessories like phone chargers and cases are most common (16%) among tech-related packages stolen. They are followed by audio gadgets like headphones and Bluetooth speakers, along with streaming devices and soundbars (11%, respectively). 

Still, more costly tech like gaming consoles (10%), computers and laptops (9%) and smart home devices (6%) are among devices stolen.

Cole Kan / CNET

You shouldn’t leave your packages up to chance. That’s why Lacoma recommends a few safer options to ensure your packages are stored securely after they’re delivered, even beyond keeping an eye on your doorbell or security camera. Instead, keep your packages out of sight with tactics like a delivery box with a code or key or ask for an in-garage delivery. 

“Delivery boxes have reached a new level of popularity in recent years as an effective way to stop porch pirates completely. However, Amazon’s Key service that delivers to your garage is an alternative,” said Lacoma. “Either way, you’ll need to trust delivery people to handle your shipments, unless you want to arrange for pickup at a nearby shipping center, which some people like to combine with other holiday errands.”

If you don’t want to install a new security feature, try scheduling your packages to arrive when you know you’re home, requiring a signature from someone you trust or changing your delivery location to a pickup spot, like UPS’ Hold for Pick-Up locations or Amazon Lockers. 

How US adults really feel about home security tech

Home surveillance, like outdoor security cameras and video doorbells, can deter package thieves who don’t want to risk getting caught on camera. But US adults have mixed feelings about their effectiveness in protecting against package theft. 

There are two deterrents that are keeping US adults from having security devices — cost and privacy. Findings show that 20% of US adults lack home security measures due to hardware costs or monthly subscription fees. That’s followed by 9% who don’t want to use cameras because of privacy concerns. 

“Fortunately, the right home security picks can solve both these problems,” said Lacoma. “Brands like Tapo, Eufy, Aqara and even Google Nest offer package detection and alerts for free, so you don’t have to worry about extra fees.” 

Lacoma added that many companies also offer ways to use local video storage and local AI detection so nothing is stored in the cloud. There are also features, such as customizable privacy zones, to minimize privacy concerns when used with the right precautions.

Among all US adults, only 14% have security devices with a monthly subscription that lets them save or playback video. By comparison, 12% have security devices but no subscription. 

Those percentages could be low for a few reasons, including the overall perception of how helpful surveillance and security really are against porch theft. Eleven percent of US adults don’t think security devices deter porch thefts. It’s a valid concern since 4% fell victim to package theft or an attempted theft despite having security devices. And some US adults (9%) use security devices to get proof of a theft after the fact — not to prevent it. 

But that doesn’t mean you should ignore the possibility of package theft — especially during the holidays. Even if you don’t want to install cameras or new security devices, make a plan to protect your packages and avoid the headache of package theft over the holidays. 

“Remember, the simple presence of a security camera is enough to make many thieves look elsewhere – interviews have confirmed it,” said Lacoma. “And with today’s phone alerts about package detection, you can usually check on a package only seconds after it appears, or bring up footage if it unexpectedly vanishes, letting you take action fast. New practices like delivery boxes or in-garage delivery help address risks in concrete ways, too.”

Methodology

CNET commissioned YouGov Plc to conduct the survey. All figures, unless otherwise stated, are from YouGov Plc. The total sample size was 2,016 adults. Fieldwork was undertaken between Oct. 23–27, 2026. The survey was carried out online. The figures have been weighted and are representative of all US adults (aged 18 plus).

The $75 billion figure was calculated by multiplying the average value of deliveries each US adult expects to receive by the 2025 US population of adults ages 18 and over calculated by the US Census Bureau.

Dashia investigates economic shifts and everyday challenges to help readers make well-informed decisions, and she covers a range of topics, including technology, security, energy and money. snippet: Everyone has that traveler in their life. That person who feels more at home on a 14-hour train ride than a quiet Sunday on the couch. They speak multiple languages, have a gut like a goat, and make friends wherever they go. Whether they're your kindred spirit or the person you live vicariously through, one thing never changes: They always need new gear. That's what makes travelers so fun to buy for. But you don't want to get them just anything. The key is to find that clever gift even they didn't know they needed, and that's where we come in. From streaming gadgets for the hotel to portable espresso makers and high-capacity charger … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
Everyone has that traveler in their life. That person who feels more at home on a 14-hour train ride than a quiet Sunday on the couch. They speak multiple languages, have a gut like a goat, and make friends wherever they go. Whether they’re your kindred spirit or the person you live vicariously through, one thing never changes: They always need new gear.

That’s what makes travelers so fun to buy for. But you don’t want to get them just anything. The key is to find that clever gift even they didn’t know they needed, and that’s where we come in. From streaming gadgets for the hotel to portable espresso makers and high-capacity chargers, these are our favorite gifts to help travelers take their next adventure to the next level.

Presented by: Delta

Give Yourself A Gift With Holiday Travel Deals. Make the most of the season with limited-time holiday offers on travel and more. However you choose to celebrate, explore more ways to save and make your next journey even more rewarding. Terms apply. Ends December 15, 2026.

How much do you want to spend?

$1495

It’s time for a smarter robovac. Thankfully, there’s the Matic, which looks less like the rambling discs that pervade the space and more like an actual robot that, well, vacuums. It doesn’t get under beds, but it also doesn’t get stuck under them, and it does a great job providing truly no-fuss cleaning thanks to its superb mapping.

$18

One charging port, two phones. That’s not a problem with Anker’s dual-headed USB-C cable, which offers either 4 or 6 feet of length to provide game-changing versatility when you need it most.

$80

Built for jet setters, Anker’s 100W travel adapter features a durable design, a handy LCD display to track charge percentage, and compatibility in over 200 countries. It doesn’t support AC plugs, but it does have four USB inputs for all your portables, including a trio of USB-C ports.

$599

Who says you can’t travel with a big screen? The Xreal One Pro feature dual micro-OLED displays to project a virtual 171-inch screen from your device of choice. A 57-degree field of view, max 120Hz refresh rate, and built-in speakers round things out, delivering portable cinematic entertainment for one.

$13

For frequent flyers, a plain suitcase sticker may not be enough. In the age of QR codes, Pebblebee’s Link Bag Tags make a lot more sense. They’re battery-free, scannable by anyone with a phone, and offer built-in privacy with the ability to share or deny personal information.

$179

Apple’s AirPods Pro are the epitome of wireless earbud refinement, with fantastic noise-canceling and transparency modes, a light and airy fit, and clear sound thanks to ear tips that seal your ears without plugging them up. The latest pair continues the quest for perfection with faster processing, more features, and better ergonomics than ever.

$399

Oura didn’t reinvent the wheel with the Ring 5, but it did reshape it into a slimmer, thinner, more wearable design that could make all the difference. Inside are the same extensive health and fitness-tracking features for charting everything from sleep to heart health, backed by long battery life.

$21

Whether you’re white-water rafting or trekking through a damp jungle, keeping your gear dry is essential. The Sea to Summit dry bag is a slick, affordable solution with clever features, including a reflective interior and a D-ring buckle to secure it to boats and bikes. The solid warranty is just a plus.

$95

SwitchBot’s powerful, battery-powered fan is a big upgrade over your average plug-in. As a 3D circulator, it can tilt to push air in all directions. You can also control it via an app, and it even detaches from its stand to sit on a desk or tabletop. Quiet and versatile, it’s equipped for nearly any adventure on or off the grid.

$55

Espresso in the woods? Yes, please. The GR2’s magical mechanics make it possible, letting you turn 12 ounces of grounds into espresso without power. Its carrying case houses all the accessories needed to get that sweet shot of bean, making real coffee available virtually anywhere.

$260

You can’t project anything anywhere from your phone or watch (yet), but the Aurzen Zip makes that moment feel closer. Bright and durable, the foldable projector can mirror content from your phone or tablet on most flat surfaces, but fair warning: It doesn’t work with streaming services like Netflix without a $129.99 CastPlay HDMI dongle.

$220

Theragun’s latest therapeutic cure for sore muscles is as packable as it is luxurious. The third-gen Mini includes clever features like a travel lock to keep it off during transport, guided routines, and USB-C charging. There’s even a Y2K edition for the ’90s kid in all of us.

$30

Every traveler needs a go-to backpack, and the Uniqlo Utility stands out for all the little things. Its minimalist, water-resistant design hides plenty of pockets on the front and sides, plus a roomy laptop sleeve and extras, including a handy key holder in the front pocket.

$46

For travelers hitting the road when the thermometer is rising, cooling off is essential. Nitecore’s long-lasting izzCool 10 Pro offers heat relief with a powerful fan and fillable reservoir that mists you for a refreshing respite from the sun. It even works with larger containers to double as a nighttime humidifier.

$298

Every traveler needs quality noise-canceling for long flights, but flagship headphones are becoming increasingly spendy. Sony’s former flagship WH-1000XM4 were so good, they’ve been bestsellers through two new generations. Now the company has revamped them in the XM4C, adding minor improvements to a stone-cold classic at a nice price.

$84

Packing light is essential for all travelers, but it’s particularly vital for those who trek long distances. This high-capacity Nitecore charger is a killer addition to any pack, with water resistance, fast charging, and a slim, lightweight design that can power your devices without weighing them down.

$499

The Switch 2 leverages the same ideas as its predecessor, only with a larger, 7.9-inch display, a faster chip, and a bevy of new social features. However, its most important trait is that it’s the newest Nintendo console, which means access to a host of weird, beautiful, family-friendly games that only Nintendo could dream up, now on a better screen.

$25

Every traveler’s been there. You get to the hotel or rental place, go to plug in your gear, and there’s only one outlet available. Fortunately, Tessan’s pack-friendly power strip offers all the ports, with multiple USB-C, USB-A, and AC inputs to charge everything in one place.

$50

If you have an avid road tripper on your list, Ugreen’s four-port car charger blends slick design with serious utility. More importantly, it has a built-in retractable USB-C cable that delivers up to 60W of power and keeps things tidy.

$10

For the fastidious person on your list who can’t stop polishing their camera, tablet, or other delicate piece of equipment, there’s the lightweight Magic Wrap. The foldable, plush fabric sticks to itself, with no zippers, edges, or even magnets to scuff or scratch your most precious gear.

$600

For on-the-go creators, it’s all about capturing the moment in the highest video quality possible. Insta360’s Luna Pro steadycam offers plenty of features to get the job done right, including 4K vertical video, swift file transfers, four hours of battery life, and a detachable touchscreen that doubles as a remote.

$25

Buying your loved one a pair of shoes is tougher than you might think, but a gift card to The Walking Company is a step in the right direction. The store offers a wide variety of ultra-comfortable kicks, boots, sandals, and even orthotics, along with a shoe finder to help them find the right fit.

$179

Retroid has had its stumbles, but the Pocket 5 is a hit, making it a great gift for the globe-trotting gamer. With a 5.5-inch OLED screen, a light yet durable design, and tons of titles available from the Google Play Store, the portable deck provides plenty of reasons to keep playing through the runway taxi.

$20

Losing important documents on a trip can be disastrous. Bagsmart’s Blast Travel Pouch is a great way to keep them all safe, with multiple pockets, an easily adjustable strap, and even RFID blocking to deflect electronic thieves.

$19

Mechanism’s clever, durable creations are a favorite here at The Verge. The company’s foldable tray table mount is particularly brilliant, offering travelers an ergonomic way to mount devices — including larger gaming handhelds like the Steam Deck — for easy access on long flights. Just don’t forget to pick up the proper grip.

$10

Few things are more frustrating on a long flight than trying to keep your phone stable between your seasoned pretzels and fellow passengers. Thankfully, MiiKare’s adjustable, inexpensive clamp can make things less stressful for your favorite frequent flyer, so they can finally watch Olympus Has Fallen in peace.

$200

If you have a friend who constantly complains about their partner’s snoring habits, Soundcore’s Sleep A30 could be a gift they’ll never forget. With a comfy design, even for side sleepers, and advanced noise-canceling tech that actively adjusts to mask unwanted sounds, they’re a recipe for sweet, silent relief.

$110

What if you could give the gift of stress-free Wi-Fi on the go? That’s the promise of TP-Link’s dual-band Roam 7, a portable Wi-Fi 7 router that simplifies connecting to public portals so travelers can connect everything to a single device and be done with it.

$40

New parents need everything, all at once, and traveling always raises the stakes. The Hatch Go is the sound machine they’ll be thanking you for well into toddlerhood. Offering 10 soothing sounds from a crazy-compact frame with up to 15 hours of juice, it’s simple, effective, and essential.

$21

They say once you go bidet, you never go back. That’s certainly harder to achieve when traveling outside Japan, though Tushy offers an effective solution with its handy, collapsible bidet. The manual contraption isn’t heated, but one portable bathroom luxury at a time.

$75

How is your giftee supposed to bring you back something special when they’re already overpacked? The Matador Packable Duffel, of course. The durable, 30-liter carrier breaks down to micro size, then easily expands to hold loads of overseas paraphernalia. It’s a win-win!

$33

Whether your favorite traveler is a packing nerd or a slob who’s always losing everything (we’re not here to judge), everyone can use a little extra organization. Cocoon’s Grid-It accessories store it all, from chargers and gadgets to makeup and passports, with flexible straps to lock it all in.

$30

We all tend to skimp on simple items for ourselves, which is why this fancy-pants sleep mask makes such a thoughtful present. Its 3D contoured fit is designed to block all light while providing plush memory foam comfort so your loved one can get the rest they need between adventures.
