title: Disney just launched 3D movies on the Meta Quest ahead of Meta VR Glasses’ release
snippet: All available 3D movies are included with your Disney+ subscription and come with extras you can only experience in VR. more…
fullText:
All available 3D movies are included with your Disney+ subscription and come with extras you can only experience in VR.

See the Monsters, Inc. Scare Floor above? That’s an actual environment you could be in right now on your Meta Quest headset while watching Monsters, Inc. in 3D. Disney+ now offers all subscribers a selection of 3D movies when you use the Disney+ app on a Meta Quest headset. Only Dolby Atmos and Dolby Vision capabilities are locked behind specific subscription tiers, not the movies themselves. Meta says the library includes over 60 3D movies, and more are coming when Meta VR Glasses launch in Spring 2027.

While 3D movies on a VR headset are uniquely amazing (much more convincing than 3D TV ever was), the most exciting part of the Meta Quest experience is the immersive environments. Disney and Meta worked together to create a fully unique movie-watching experience that gives movies more than just the depth that 3D movies typically have; you’ll also be watching the movies in an environment that’s unique and changes throughout the movie.

Meta says you can “Catch Star Wars: A New Hope (Episode IV) from a comfy spot on Tatooine, see the Avengers battle Loki from atop Avengers Tower, settle in for a Pixar movie night on the Monsters, Inc. Scare Floor, and more.” Some of these immersive environments were shown off at Meta Connect in September when Meta VR Glasses were announced, but it’s a bit surprising to see so many of them launch months ahead of VR Glasses’ retail debut.

	

Disney also highlights IMAX experiences, which are also available in the Disney+ app on Meta Quest headsets. These movies mimic the full IMAX experience in VR by putting you in a virtual theater with a massive screen, all at the correct IMAX aspect ratio. Rumor also has it that Meta will include other 3D movies with its Meta VR+ subscription service.

If you’re not subscribed to Disney+ yet, you may be able to get a free trial so you can check out all the new movies available with every subscription tier. And if you don’t have a Meta Quest headset yet, we’re fully expecting it to go on sale for Black Friday this year, which looks to be starting earlier than ever this year, if other early Black Friday deals are any indication.

by  Andrew Liszewski

Nov 18, 2026, 4:00 PM UTC

Image: 8BitDo

Andrew Liszewski

 

is a senior reporter who’s been covering and reviewing the latest gadgets and tech since 2006, but has loved all things electronic since he was a kid.

The 8BitDo 64 was a loose remake of the Nintendo 64’s unusual triple-grip controller that did away with that gamepad’s centered analog stick. But with its new GC Bluetooth Gamepad, 8BitDo has done a much better job at staying faithful to the design of the Nintendo GameCube’s excellent controllers, including their unique button layout, thumbstick design, and shoulder buttons.

The 8BitDo GC Bluetooth Gamepad is available for preorder starting today for $49.99 in orange or purple and is expected to start shipping on December 10th. That’s much cheaper than Nintendo’s $69.99 wireless remake of the GameCube controller, although 8BitDo’s version isn’t an exact copy of the original’s shape and ergonomics. If that’s important to you, and you have your GameCube’s original accessories on hand, you can still buy 8BitDo’s $25.98 upgrade kit, which is a cheaper way to make it compatible with modern consoles and devices.

8BitDo’s GameCube redux carries forward the original’s octagonal gates around the base of each thumbstick, making it well-suited to playing fighting games like Super Smash Bros. Ultimate. And while Nintendo continues to skip modern thumbstick technologies, the 8BitDo GC features both drift-resistant TMR thumbsticks and Hall effect linear triggers.

The controller connects to all versions of the Nintendo Switch over Bluetooth, as well as PCs or handheld consoles running Windows. It also comes with a 2.4GHz wireless USB receiver for players who prefer a connection with lower latency, or you can connect it with a USB-C cable for the best possible performance.

title: GTA 6 Review: The Megayacht of Gaming Has Something for Nearly Everyone
snippet: Over a decade in the making, GTA 6 is a colossal, polished game with a core love story about the American dream: Doing enough crime to retire early.
fullText:
The most anticipated game in recent history, Grand Theft Auto 6, lives up to the hype. Expansive, interactive and peppered with so much to do that it’s easy to sink scores of hours into the launch game — and who knows how much more will be added later on. 

GTA 6 iterates on the grandness of its predecessor, and in the 13 years since GTA 5 stretched gamer expectations with a huge map of seemingly endless activities, developer Rockstar Games has figured out how to layer a lot of granular detail into its next canvas of crime and carnage. 

Environments that were sketched out in the last game, such as stores and buildings, are detailed and explorable. Bystanders and police react more naturally to your presence and culpability — cops now have to see you escaping the crime scene to tag you as a suspect for pursuit. You can talk people down from fights. And the game’s titular transgression of stealing cars is more nuanced than ever. 

			

More from CNET

	

		

	

									

									

						

		

				

			Rockstar/CNET		

	

		

							

											

							Available now						

											

															GTA 6 at Amazon

			Rockstar/CNET

			Get it now		

	

		
		

			

If you prefer, you can preorder your copy of GTA 6 from Walmart.

		

	

Granted, early versions of some of these advancements were explored in Rockstar’s interim game, 2018’s Red Dead Redemption 2, and the series iteratively progressed with all the updates that continue to this day for GTA Online, which was built out from GTA 5 to be an ever-evolving game-as-a-service. But they’ve been taken to the next level in GTA 6, leading to a world that feels more responsive to your presence and actions. With all its systems, map space and activities, it feels like the megayacht of gaming — a polished experience in all its corners, with some of the most detailed graphics you’ll find in gaming.

A lot of that rests on the shoulders of the game’s protagonists, lovers in crime Lucia and Jason, who operate radically differently from previous GTA point-of-view characters. Their romance (if players choose to pursue it) offers a whole new narrative and systematic view of a life outside the law, with collaborative and solo missions that paint a vivid picture of the playful, dangerous world of GTA. Outside story missions, casually driving around as a couple fills the dead air with conversation and the robberies with partnered backup, enriched by their growing relationship, lathering their activities with all the sweetness of a violent date night.

The couple’s story is a very lengthy affair — at 50 hours in, the game says I’ve completed roughly 70% of it — and is robust enough to justify the price of entry. It’s a compelling narrative about two people trying to build a future through a dangerous world by leaning deeper into the danger, but it’s also a showcase of the world Rockstar built. After the story is done, the game hands you the keys to explore it yourself however you’d like.

GTA 6’s world is large, consisting of multiple counties with their own character and environments, all based on the Miami area of Florida.

Rockstar declined to comment on whether GTA 6 will transition into the next version of GTA Online, but it feels like an inevitability. It’s hard to ignore the vast space, systems and mechanics that players only briefly dabble with while playing through the story. From fishing to treasure hunting in underwater shipwrecks to big game hunting to street racing, there’s a lot of low-stakes fodder to unwind with the game — and plenty of bank heists, chases and other random crimes to ratchet up the tension, too.

At launch, GTA 6 has a broad foundation of things to do that — I suspect — will increase over time. It’s layered with Rockstar’s signature puerile humor, and I’ll fess up to laughing at some of the frequent boner jokes and crass names (one sportscar brand is the “pfister”), but the occasional homophobia and transphobia is bizarrely out of time — the game’s mock-everything culture still feels rooted in the 2000s, aimed at people who loved the edginess of South Park in its heyday. More modern satire appears in bystander conversations that range into absurd caricatures of far-right anti-woke crusaders and rabid leftists, but given the game’s faux-Florida setting in the fictional state of Leonida (which includes the legendary Vice City), there’s far more of the former than the latter. 

Thus, the world feels textured even for players just picking up the game to fool around. While there are sparse stretches of the map, little side stories unfold for those who notice and follow strange things afoot. But a massive part of the game’s appeal and heart lies in the ballad of two lovebirds, kept apart by immaturity and circumstance but brought together through crime and the skewed American dream at the center of every GTA: Pull off a big enough heist and the world is yours.

Screenshot by David Lumb/CNET

The romance and partnership of Jason and Lucia

The game’s story opens from Jason’s perspective — a twentysomething guy, former military, quiet and gruff, drifting through life doing odd jobs for a small-time kingpin out in the sticks. A little drug-running and skirmishing with the local gangs keep him busy, working out and drinking beers on his deck, watching the sunset from GTA 6’s version of the Florida Keys.

All that changes when Lucia, who stole and then broke his heart, gets out of prison on early release and asks to crash with him during her parole. A tenuous second chance is complicated when she reconnects with a former cellmate who’s partnered with a rich hotshot dangling wealth in front of our fragile couple. This could be the ticket to a financial foundation to help them start anew. Then a job goes wrong, and the pair go on the run, restarting in a rural backwater as far from the clubs of Vice City as one can get. 

This is where players decide how close they want Jason and Lucia to be. The game sets up the beginnings of their reconnection, but they can drift apart if players don’t choose to bring them closer. It’s all about the little things: Jason holding the door for Lucia, one of them buying clothes for the other at the vendor, or even just sidling close during morning coffee. Rockstar didn’t want to force players into this relationship — even if things fizzle, the pair will still go through the game as partners in crime, doing jobs together even if they sleep apart. 

But players will value something if they have to work for it, Rob Nelson, head of development at Rockstar North, told me over a video call. He likened the couple’s relationship to how players embraced the honor system in RDR2, with more taking the high honor route than being a vicious criminal. 

“When you can lose something, it’s more meaningful if you work to keep it,” Nelson said. 

As Nelson explained, Rockstar came off of GTA 5’s story with its three protagonists wondering how to one-up it for the sequel, which started development soon after in 2015 but took until early 2019 to settle on GTA 6’s main pair. A romantic couple is indeed a step up from characters who come together for a job and split after, and Rockstar had to figure out how that’s different for lovers — they’re not going to end a job at 2 a.m. and part ways; they’re going home to go to bed, Nelson said. 

The couple essentially have a run-on conversation that lasts through the story, piping up during long drives to chat about a recent mission or bring up something from their pasts. How much these topics are tailored to events and how much are randomly chosen feels cleverly obscured, coming off like the natural chatter between two people slowly figuring each other out. The sheer scale of the recorded dialogue dwarfs other games and becomes a feature among many, showcasing the titanic work Rockstar put into GTA 6. 

It all adds up to a compelling narrative centered on two characters, carefully chiseled to embody the best and worst of Vice City, inspired by the real-life Bonnie and Clyde and by crime couples from films like True Romance and Natural Born Killers. GTA 6’s couple starts with a meet-cute over trying to steal the same car, and freshly out of prison, Lucia eggs on Jason to take bigger illegal jobs than the small-time gigs he’s coasted on. Even with an ankle monitor and picking up road trash on work duty, Lucia never seriously considers staying on the right side of the law. Jason is cautious about new opportunities, but eager not to lose Lucia again, and never considers going straight.

Jason and Lucia can be a couple if players keep them together, but they’ll remain partners in crime regardless. Screenshot by David Lumb/CNET

Nestled within their stories is a serious point about the futility of staying honest in a city and system that caters to the rich and punishes the desperate. A flashback shows Lucia juggling gig economy rideshare driving and having her utilities shut off after failed payments, which is heartbreakingly real. But it’s a blip amid the overwhelming focus on a criminal romance, where the only escape from poverty is to steal big bills until finally retiring to a distant island beyond the consequences of your felonious lifestyle.

It’s not surprising — that’s the GTA fantasy, after all — but it’s telling which things Rockstar took great pains to update to modern tastes over the game’s decade-plus development (and what it left out). Smartphones are a huge part of the game’s social interactions, from texting and calling contacts to Instagram-like social media feeds to summoning cars through an app or hailing a ride. But notably absent are any gig economy services that have normalized atypical incomes — you can’t TaskRabbit or Uber your way to an honest living in GTA 6. Odd jobs come as under-the-table favors you do for the rich and powerful, frequently taking advantage of both protagonists’ gray morals. 

Though it won’t give you the option of a legal living, GTA 6 leans into the injustice of the wealth gap, putting a few city blocks between gang-riddled run-down apartments and the high-rise clubs populated by ignorant rich assholes. The game gleefully showcases the hypocrisy of the privileged — one time, I rushed into a rural, well-off house where a wife espousing family values ushered me to help her dying husband… who was choking in a BDSM leather harness. Once freed, he tucked his tail back into his submissive role as a “liberal cuck” for their roleplay. 

This kind of edginess-for-laughs is peppered around the game, and it’s hard not to feel the cynicism. I can de-escalate some situations, but a lot of the non-player characters you run into on the street are on a hair-trigger eager to fight. You’ll overhear plenty of anti-immigrant screeds from random bystanders. Junkies try to break into your car if you have contraband in the trunk.

If GTA 5 was released in the waning Obama years with waning public optimism, GTA 6 launches halfway into Trump’s second term, where far-right government ICE deportations and street killings have polarized the nation beyond anything we’ve seen in decades. Yet when I asked how Rockstar had adjusted the game over its long development to suit this moment, Nelson said that Jason and Lucia’s story is a counterweight of optimism and care amid all the crime and societal disparity in the game.

“Choosing love is a bit of an act of rebellion against a narcissistic culture,” Nelson said. “The ideas of selfishness and selflessness put through this world is interesting to us, giving you goals other than just maxing out your bank account with supercars and properties.” 

GTA 6’s storytelling is amplified by hundreds of animations — kisses, hugs, handshakes and fist bumps.Screenshot by David Lumb/CNET

How  tech upgrades and new systems make GTA 6 the megayacht of games

Evaluating a game with so much detail spread across a vast map area is difficult, as the polish can be mistaken for quality. When I parked in a narrow driveway, I noticed Jason has an entire animation for shimmying through a slim gap. There have to be a dozen sequences for ways he and Lucia can sidle up to each other for a quick peck or embrace, all optional. There must be a thousand or more buildings you can duck into to explore their interiors. And the amount of dialogue feels unfathomably colossal, all voiced with aplomb by talented actors.

Where other games have some, GTA 6 has more. It’s a little like asking whether a megayacht is enjoyable to commute to work. The simple answer is yes, GTA 6 is an incredible game. And yet, its scope can be distracting. Halfway through the story, I was zipping from destroying drug dens to stealing valuable cars for a collector to hunting big game in the rural hills — all good fun, but my attention easily peeled away from the main story and the couple’s attempt to secure their financial independence, retire early future. The prior chapter had ended in a gun battle as hired killers came for a dangerous MacGuffin in Jason and Lucia’s hands, but amid all the good, clean street crime, that danger had receded to the background.

Diving for sunken treasure in shipwrecks is one of the many, many things that occupy the player’s time in GTA 6. Screenshot by David Lumb/CNET

The story’s punch is diluted by everything you can and probably will do, which feels like forgetting the taste of the prime rib after sampling everything else at a buffet. But at least all those activities are enjoyable and round out the criminal with the casual, including mini golf and mud races far from the dense urban core of Vice City. It’s like if Lego Island grew up to add larceny to its roster of fun things to do. 

In grappling with the scale of the game, I repeatedly reach for simile — too many options make it harder to fully define GTA 6 and who it’s for, outside of saying there’s so much that its appeal spreads very wide. There’s not quite something for everyone, but it offers such a plethora of side activities that if one gets tiring, another will probably tide you over. This is what will most likely form the foundation of an eventual transition to GTA Online: A substantial stream of things to do on top of stacking cash. And given GTAO’s sustained success, the baseline version of GTA 6 will please all the heist junkies and freeform adventurers who’ve loved the series, even if they aren’t hooked by the well-crafted core story. All the looky-loos curious about the hype will find one of the most polished and visually gorgeous video games ever made.

GTA fans will notice a lot of small improvements that clean up logical inconsistencies. Witnesses have to notice you doing a crime to report it, and cops have to see you flee a crime scene to put out an all-points bulletin on your description, though you can lower your chances of being recognized by swapping outfits and respraying the color of your getaway ride. 

Working out will increase your health and stamina meters, and exercising as a couple keeps you close.Screenshot by David Lumb/CNET

Other new features add complexity to the game. Certain crimes are riskier until you get new tools and connections unlocked through the story, which let you steal cars with trackers and rob banks with countermeasures. Exercise and diet affect your health and physique, which you’ll need to maintain with regular workouts. You can steal guns and vehicles, but they won’t be saved unless you pay to buy or register them, respectively.

These sound tedious, but they’re little frictions that make living in the world of GTA 6 more intentional. Early in the game as Jason, I frequently found myself waking up in the morning, grabbing a cup of coffee and doing a workout to get my in-game day “started,” putting on the radio and feeding my snake or checking in with Lucia ambling around the kitchen. As the relationship between the two deepens, they can go to bed together, cuddled up and doomscrolling on their phones.

Romance means scrolling on your phones together.Screenshot by David Lumb/CNET

The emergent adventures in a game world bristling with systems

While I expect a million posts of “he just like me fr fr” to blanket social media as people wonder at the work Rockstar put in to replicate our (often terrible) habits, there’s still a lot I was delighted to discover that’s unique to the world they’ve made. Some of these are jokes taken to an extreme, like the intentionally pretentious game-within-a-game you can play, Tenebrae Lux — a black-and-white walking simulator by an in-universe auteur, Johannes Zuch, whose name flashes on the screen so many times that it feels like a wink toward Hideo Kojima and other famous game creators.

“We love auteurs — it’s not mocking, it’s celebrating,” Nelson said.

But my favorite things in any GTA game are the side stories you can chance upon that are scripted but feel emergent, exploring the bizarre nooks and crannies of the world. One night halfway through the game, I was casually driving around as Lucia when I saw a police chopper aiming a spotlight at the street — and found the cops in a standoff with a man in a fox suit. 

When being your furry self is a literal crime, the only option is to break the law.Screenshot by David Lumb/CNET

I immediately discovered that, in the game’s fictional state of Leonida, being a furry (e.g., wearing a fursuit and expressing your fursona) is illegal, so I broke through the police blockade to liberate him. I met up with his fellow furries and spirited them away to a compound, during which I peeked over my shoulder to find them nuzzling each other. God bless you little oddballs bravely living your truth in the face of unjust laws.

Like its forebears, GTA 6 feels like two games — a core narrative about making a living through the underground in a rags-to-riches-to-rags-to-riches saga of a star-crossed couple, and a massive sandbox to do whatever you want. While going treasure hunting in offshore wrecks or making drug drop-offs from a plane dilutes the story’s tension, it also gives you a lot of opportunity to find the GTA you want to experience. After the story fades into memory, that’s what’ll stick around as the core of this game: the freedom to choose what you want to do, laws be damned. 

Eventually, you’ll face that ultimate temptation to cause such havoc that you’ll trigger the game’s new, sixth star of police attention — one in which it feels like every cop in Leonida is coming after you, and it doesn’t stop until you’re arrested or put down, a countdown to how long Jason and Lucia can stick it to the law at maximum volume.

“I haven’t played six stars since we finalized it, I made it too long so we made it harder,” Nelson said. “I’m curious to see what times people get!”

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

David Lumb

											David Lumb is a managing editor for the mobile team, covering mobile and gaming spaces. Before CNET, he covered tech, gaming, and culture for TechRadar, Engadget, Popular Mechanics, NBC Asian America, Increment, Fast Company and others. As a true Californian, he lives for coffee, beaches and burritos.

excerpt:
The most anticipated game in recent history, Grand Theft Auto 6, lives up to the hype. Expansive, interactive and peppered with so much to do that it’s easy to sink scores of hours into the launch game — and who knows how much more will be added later on.

GTA 6 iterates on the grandness of its predecessor, and in the 13 years since GTA 5 stretched gamer expectations with a huge map of seemingly endless activities, developer Rockstar Games has figured out how to layer a lot of granular detail into its next canvas of crime and carnage.

title: ‘Lenovo Googlebook Duet 13’ leak points to January launch [Gallery]
snippet: Google teased last month that detachable Googlebooks are coming soon, and a leak today provides the best look at the “Lenovo Googlebook Duet 13” yet. more…
fullText:
Google teased last month that detachable Googlebooks are coming soon, and a leak today provides the best look at the “Lenovo Googlebook Duet 13” yet.

This follows the first leak in July that showed a 2-in-1 tablet and two laptops, with the Lenovo Googlebook 15 launching in October.

Evan Blass today shared more images of the “Lenovo Googlebook Duet 13” and noted that it is “launching in January.” Notably, the branding builds on Lenovo’s Chromebook Duet lineup, while we get confirmation of the 13-inch screen.

The top-down view shows the detachable keyboard with keys that feature a bottom curvature, like on the available Lenovo device. We see a trackpad that is on the smaller side, while “Googlebook” appears below the Ctrl key. This image also shows the stylus.

	
	

Blass previously shared images in September that showed a physical switch at the right edge of the keyboard, while the pen magnetically attaches and charges when docked on the top edge.

There’s a pill-shaped cutout at the top-right edge that might be a curiously placed USB-C port. It’s not the power button as that’s on the left edge, which is home to another USB-C connector at the bottom.

The removable back cover stand looks to be magnetic and has a diagonal fold with rather prominent “Lenovo” branding. The Glowbar is placed next to the camera on the rear side.

The rumored January launch would align with a CES 2027 announcement. It would serve as the next big moment for Googlebooks, with Google spending the last few weeks on bug fixes and improvements.

title: Google Voice appears to finally be working on RCS support
snippet: It might finally be happening. A new Google Voice update plants seeds of RCS support, though the exact details remain unclear. more…
fullText:
It might finally be happening. A new Google Voice update plants seeds of RCS support, though the exact details remain unclear.

About APK Insight: In this “APK Insight” post, we’ve decompiled the latest version of an application that Google uploaded to the Play Store. When we decompile these files (called APKs, in the case of Android apps), we’re able to see various lines of code within that hint at possible future features. Keep in mind that Google may or may not ever ship these features, and our interpretation of what they are may be imperfect. We’ll try to enable those that are closer to being finished, however, to show you how they’ll look in case that they do ship. With that in mind, read on.

Google Voice is an invaluable tool for accessing one phone number across a host of different devices, but to say it’s becoming less impactful without support for RCS is a bit of an understatement. Now that virtually every Android phone and iPhone supports the new messaging experience, Google Voice is less useful both for business and consumer users.

But that seems to be changing.

	

Google Voice for Android version 2026.11.01.1014278023 doesn’t enable RCS, but it does, for the first time, actually hint that the functionality might be on its way. In a teardown of the app, one simple string stands out:

<string name=”message_send_button_rcs”>RCS</string>

That points to a new send button used for RCS messages rather than SMS. Google Messages similarly changes its send button to differentiate between the two standards. 

	

This update contains a host of other new strings around images, videos, and more, but none of them are directly tied to RCS support. 

The folks over at Android Authority dug up some other tidbits about RCS including an “RCS chat preference” toggle and various RCS actions and messages. But, again, nothing is live just yet, and there’s no word on when it might arrive, if ever.

Google has been championing RCS support for over a decade now, so it’s long past due for Voice, a long-running Google product, to get on board. While the tidbits in this update don’t serve as any confirmation RCS if coming to Voice, it’s the most exciting update on the matter in years.

title: Why iPhone Duo wasn’t for me (but might be for you)
snippet: I’ve had the iPhone Duo for nearly two weeks now, and have officially decided to return it. Here are the three main reasons why the Duo didn’t work out for me, but might for you. more…
fullText:
I’ve had the iPhone Duo for nearly two weeks now, and have officially decided to return it. Here are the three main reasons why the Duo didn’t work out for me, but might for you.

#1: One-handed use is my default

I use my iPhone one-handed all the time, and based on my experience, iPhone Duo is clearly intended to be used with two hands. You can use it one-handed, but for me it’s not nearly as comfortable as the iPhone 18 Pro. It’s too wide and too heavy to be used for long.

Perhaps over time I’d get used to needing two hands for most iPhone interactions. But that would be a pretty significant shift for me, as there are so many situations when I don’t have both hands free.

If you already use two hands with your iPhone regularly—perhaps because you have a Pro Max model—then the Duo’s one-handed experience likely won’t bother you. But the more I used the Duo, the more I found myself missing my iPhone 18 Pro.

#2: The inner display didn’t draw me in

The biggest value proposition of a foldable is that it’s a 2-in-1 product, letting you have a standard phone but also a tablet-sized display that fits in your pocket.

I totally get the appeal, and fully expected to love that hybrid design. But after two weeks of trying, I still struggled to find times when I actually wanted to unfold the Duo. And to be clear, that’s a me problem, not an issue with the Duo itself.

I tried a bunch of apps on the inner display, and struggled to find use cases that—for me—made it worthwhile to open the Duo. But based on the feedback I’ve seen from most Duo owners, I’m very much in the minority.

I know lots of people love the Duo for video, but I don’t watch much video on my iPhone. I almost never watch YouTube, TikTok, or Instagram Reels. And for shows and movies, I stick with my TV screen and an Apple TV 4K.

Multitasking support on iPhone Duo works really well. But when I found myself needing to multitask, I still reached for my iPad Pro with Magic Keyboard attached. A keyboard-free product can’t replace my main computer (nor would I expect it to), and the Duo screen was too small to comfortably work on it.

#3: I want the best camera system

Last year I bought an iPhone Air and absolutely loved it. Initially, the Air’s less capable camera system didn’t bother me, it was “good enough.”

After a few months though, I started missing the Pro camera system more. Then I learned that my wife was pregnant with twins, and I knew I wanted the best possible iPhone cameras to capture their early weeks and months. So I bought an iPhone 18 Pro in September.

I’ve been very impressed by iPhone 18 Pro’s Main camera upgrades, and it’s great having a Telephoto lens again too. Since having the best camera system is so crucial for me right now, I knew iPhone Duo couldn’t be my only iPhone.

I initially planned to dual-carry the two models, using iPhone 18 Pro solely as a camera. But over and over I found myself wishing it was my only iPhone.

	

Is the iPhone Duo camera good enough for most people? Probably so. But for this year at least, with my twins aging rapidly, it’s not quite right for me. If I loved the Duo for other reasons, I would just use both models. But since I didn’t, I’m happy to stick with the iPhone 18 Pro.

iPhone Duo wrap-up: This is not a bad review

In closing, I want to explicitly state that I don’t think the iPhone Duo is a bad product, and this isn’t a “bad review.”

The iPhone Duo just isn’t for me. I get the sense, though, that it’s lots of people’s favorite iPhone in years. Apple created its most unique new iPhone model since the original, and there’s plenty to love about it. I’m very curious to see how popular foldables become over time compared to slab models, because each clearly offers pros and cons. But for me, at least right now, the iPhone 18 Pro is my model of choice.

What has your iPhone Duo experience been like so far? Love it? Undecided? Let us know in the comments.

title: The Google Wallet app is now available on iOS
snippet: Google Wallet is now available on iOS to “organize purchases, tickets, boarding passes, and more in one easy place” in the US. more…
fullText:
Google Wallet is now available on iOS to “organize purchases, tickets, boarding passes, and more in one easy place” in the US.

The Google Wallet app on iPhone does not offer tap-to-pay functionality due to platform restrictions. Instead, Google touts three intended use cases:

“Digitize your physical cards. Quickly scan loyalty cards and gym memberships using your phone’s camera to import them into Google Wallet.”

App navigation is handled by a floating pill (in Liquid Glass) with two tabs. The homepage starts with a carousel of recent purchases slated for delivery, followed by boarding passes, and finally a grid of loyalty cards.

“Securely manage payment cards to check out faster online across Google and anywhere you use Google Pay.”

The next tab shows a list of recent transactions associated with Google. The Wallet app will display purchase emails and summarize them. You also get a list of Passes, which you can pin/unpin from the homepage, and payment methods saved to your Google Account. 

	

The ‘plus’ FAB (floating action button) lets you add loyalty, gift, and payment cards (for use in Chrome). There’s a convenient “Everything else” camera scanner that can be used to digitize anything else. 

“Stay in control of agentic purchases made across Google. Easily view and manage order confirmations, receipts, and delivery updates all in one secure place.”

The other main reason Google Wallet now exists on iOS is that the company wants the app to be a “secure hub for managing agentic purchases across Google.”

title: Epic formally asks SCOTUS to uphold contempt ruling against Apple
snippet: Epic Games has submitted its official response to Apple’s Supreme Court appeal, urging the justices to uphold the contempt ruling over App Store payment restrictions. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Epic Games has submitted its official response to Apple’s Supreme Court appeal, urging the justices to uphold the contempt ruling over App Store payment restrictions. Here are the details.

A bit of context

As most 9to5Mac readers probably know, Apple and Epic Games have been engaged in a lengthy legal battle since 2020, when Epic sued Apple after Fortnite was removed from the App Store.

The move came after Epic remotely activated an alternative payment system that bypassed Apple’s In-App Purchase system.

Although the court largely sided with Apple, it did rule that the company could no longer prevent developers from directing users to alternative payment methods outside the App Store.

Apple ultimately allowed those links, but imposed new restrictions, including a 27% commission on external purchases, in addition to new rules limiting how developers could display buttons and links to alternative payment methods.

Epic challenged those restrictions, and the court agreed that Apple had violated the original injunction, holding the company in civil contempt.

Apple has since attempted multiple times to overturn that ruling, arguing that the original injunction contained no explicit prohibition on imposing those restrictions.

Epic, on the other hand, argues that Apple deliberately circumvented the court order by introducing new rules designed to achieve the same result as those originally prohibited.

In May, Apple appealed to the Supreme Court, which agreed in June to hear the case. Apple submitted its opening brief in September, followed by supporting briefs from the U.S. government and several legal and business groups.

Those included the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, Chamber of Progress, and several former federal antitrust enforcers. In a nutshell, the U.S. government argued that the original injunction did not clearly prohibit Apple’s 27% commission on external purchases, but maintained that the company was correctly held in contempt for restricting how developers could display external payment buttons.

Today, Epic filed its official response.

Epic’s official response

In its opening brief, Apple argues, citing multiple legal precedents, that courts must enforce the letter of an injunction rather than its broader spirit.

According to the company, there was nothing in the original injunction explicitly prohibiting it from charging commissions on external purchases or imposing additional restrictions on payment links, so it should not be held in contempt for conduct that the court order did not clearly prohibit.

In its response filed today, Epic disputes Apple’s interpretation of the injunction, arguing that the company “attempts to avoid contempt by proposing an extreme legal standard.”

From the filing:

[Apple] argues that a court can find contempt only if an injunction spells out the exact practice at issue–so an injunction barring Apple’s then-existing anti-steering rules left it free to implement new ones that prevent steering just as effectively. Nothing in this Court’s precedents supports that approach, which would reduce injunctions to a never-ending game of whack-a-mole.

Epic argues that “Apple devised a plan to circumvent the injunction,” claiming that “Apple chose a rate of 27% for the commission, knowing that, when combined with the developers’ payment-handling costs (more than 3%), the rate for linked-out purchases would be higher than the rate for purchases using Apple’s payment system.”

Epic writes:

As an Apple executive admitted, every “linked-out transaction is going to be more expensive to any developer * * * than an IAP transaction at 30 percent.” Apple simultaneously commissioned a “sham” report to try to provide an economic justification for the commission; the report contained an “entirely manufactured” rationale for the 27% rate.

The company also argues that “Apple tried to cover up its scheme to circumvent the injunction” by asserting privilege over more than 57,000 documents, and points to Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers’ finding that “its Vice President of Finance ‘outright lied under oath’ when he testified about when Apple decided to impose the new commission.”

Finally, Epic asks the Supreme Court to uphold the contempt ruling against Apple or, if the justices decide to clarify the legal standard for contempt, to send the case back to the lower courts for reconsideration under that standard.

With Epic’s response now filed, Apple has until December 14 to submit its final brief before oral arguments take place on January 11, 2027.

title: Google Voice app gets a redesign on Android, and it screams RCS [Gallery]
snippet: Google Voice is a wonderful service that’s often neglected, but with RCS supposedly on the way, a new app redesign is now rolling out on Android that might as well have a big neon sign that says “RCS is coming.” more…
fullText:
Google Voice is a wonderful service that’s often neglected, but with RCS supposedly on the way, a new app redesign is now rolling out on Android that might as well have a big neon sign that says “RCS is coming.”

Google Voice is a US-only service that operates a phone number over the internet. No normal carrier, just an app tied to your Google account that gets a phone number with the ability to make calls and send/receive text messages. The latter, though, has been a point of contention for the past few years as Voice was excluded from Google’s huge push into RCS.

That might finally be changing, though. Recent updates brought mention of RCS in the app’s code.

Now, a slightly newer version (v2026-11-01-1019342246) of Google Voice has debuted a redesign for the app on Android.

	

The new look isn’t a drastic restructuring, but a huge coat of paint on an app that hasn’t seen any meaningful updates since 2023. The new look feels more modern and very much influenced by Google Messages. The text field at the bottom has a rounded design with the same “+” and camera icons found in Messages, as well as a new long-press gesture that is, again, similar to Google’s primary messaging app. The main page hasn’t been updated beyond a new, rounded search bar up top and some subtly bolder fonts.

Material You colors are hit or miss now. On a Pixel with an orange theme, that color influenced the entire UI, but on a Galaxy Z Fold 8 with a coral/blue theme, the only sign of themeing was a blue message field. 

The most important thing here is the “SMS” icon on the send button, which looks just like the button in Google Messages. In that app, it’s used as an indicator as to what type of message you’re sending – SMS or RCS. Combined with code in that other recent update directly pointing to “RCS” being used on a send button, you can absolutely tell Google Voice is finally adding this long-overdue functionality.

A timeline for RCS support in Google Voice is still unclear, but this redesign going live now certainly suggests it’s coming sooner rather than later.

I can’t wait.

title: Google’s new ‘Fast Switch’ feature leaks, lets you use one number on two Android phones
snippet: Similar to a recent iPhone feature, Google appears to be working on “Fast Switch” as a way to share one SIM and phone number on two Android phones at once, and it sounds pretty cool. more…
fullText:
Similar to a recent iPhone feature, Google appears to be working on “Fast Switch” as a way to share one SIM and phone number on two Android phones at once, and it sounds pretty cool.

Through the SIM Manager app on Android, the folks over at Android Authority noticed strings that tell a pretty clear story. 

A new feature called “Android Fast Switch” would let you “use your phone number on up to two phones,” with the SIM automatically switching to “whichever phone you unlock.” 

<string name=”companion_profile_title”>Use a SIM on two phones</string>

<string name=”companion_profile_description_prefix”>With Android Fast Switch, you can use your phone number on up to two phones. Mobile service automatically switches to whichever phone you unlock.</string>

<string name=”companion_profile_description_link”>Learn more about Android Fast Switch</string>

“Android Fast Switch” sounds nearly identical to Handoff on iPhone, a feature that lets iPhone owners share one SIM between two iPhones and quickly switch devices on the fly. 

	

Other strings explicitly say that you can “Use a SIM on two phones” and specify that both devices would need to be logged into the same Google account. One phone would be the “Primary” with the other as a “companion.”

There are still plenty of unknown details here, including what data might sync between devices as well as how carriers will respond. On iPhone, carriers either charge extra for this feature ($5 at T-Mobile, $10 at Verizon), or don’t support it at all (AT&T). We also don’t know what devices may be supported – this could easily end up as a Pixel-only affair.

	

As per usual with these early teardowns, though, the actual launch of a feature like this could be weeks, months, or even years away. Still, the idea itself is rather exciting. 

9to5Google’s Take

iPhone’s Handoff feature always sounded useful, but I personally always questioned why it would be useful on iPhone. With so little variety in hardware, the utility of switching between two iPhones seems somewhat dubious, outside of perhaps using a Mini or Air as a situational device alongside a Pro device.

On Android, the combinations are endless. It all just depends on what devices Google supports. What devices would you switch between?

snippet: Classic Google Assistant sounds for special timers are back, but the “confirm” sound for smart home commands is unexpectedly different. more…
fullText:
Classic Google Assistant sounds for special timers are back, but the “confirm” sound for smart home commands is unexpectedly different.

If you woke up to your Google Home or Nest speakers making different sounds today, you’re not alone. Last night, my wife and I noticed that the usual bedtime command we run on our Google Home speaker made a wildly different sound, and this morning brought even more surprises as I set my usual morning tea timers.

I’m not a fan of the new smart home command sounds, as I think they sound too much like error sounds versus the previous “ding” noise that was a very clear success command. I tossed together a quick compilation of a few sounds, including a pizza timer, and both the on/off commands that Gemini gives when issuing smart home commands.:

And it looks like several folks on Reddit have also received the new sounds. From what I can tell, many of the classic Google Assistant timer sounds are back, potentially including:

	

Chicken / Turkey: Gobble or clucking noise with a melody.

Bacon / Sausage / Meat: Sizzling meat sounds.

Pizza / Pasta: Italian tarantella melody.

Muffins: The “Muffin Man” jingle.

Rice: An Asian-themed jingle.

Cats: Meows and purrs.

Dog: Barks and howls.

Christmas: Jingles and holiday music.

Dinner: Dinner bells.

Washing machine: Popping bubble sounds.

Pie / Cookie / Cake: Surprised crowd voices (“Ooh” and “Ahh”).

Coffee / Tea: A cafe jingle.

TV: A ritzy Hollywood-style song.

These have been completely absent for me since Gemini replaced Google Assistant on smart speakers earlier this year. They also seem to only be enabled on some generations of speakers. My original 2017 Google Home speaker issues all generic sounds, while the new 2026 Google Home Speaker has a more complete list from above. I reached out to Google to find out if any additional sounds have been added and will update this article if I hear back.

fullText:
Apple TV today celebrated two Grammy nominations, one of which further establishes a canceled show as an unlikely awards success story. Here are the details.

Apple TV adds two more major award nominations

Earlier this year, the Broadway adaptation of Apple TV’s ‘Schmigadoon!’ won four Tony Awards, including Best Musical, making Apple TV an EGOT winner by completing its collection of Emmy, Grammy, Oscar, and Tony awards.

‘Schmigadoon!’ premiered on Apple TV in 2021 and ran for two seasons, ending in 2023. In January 2024, show creator Cinco Paul confirmed that, although the third season had already been written with 25 new songs, Apple decided not to move forward with it.

Even before the Broadway adaptation’s Tony wins in June, a May report had raised hopes for the show’s return, revisiting an earlier interview in which ‘Schmigadoon!’ creator Cinco Paul revealed that there had been discussions about reviving it.

While there have been no further updates on a potential revival since then, fans got another reason to celebrate today, as the Broadway cast recording of ‘Schmigadoon!’ has been nominated for Best Musical Theater Album at the 2027 Grammy Awards.

It will compete against CHESS the Musical, The Lost Boys, Ragtime, and Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across New York).

Additionally, ‘Widow’s Bay‘ earned a nomination for Best Score Soundtrack for Visual Media, putting composer David Fleming up against the soundtracks of ‘The Odyssey,’ ‘One Battle After Another,’ ‘Project Hail Mary,’ and ‘Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu‘.

title: SpaceX Misses Its Double Catch but Still Makes History by Catching the Starship
snippet: The Super Heavy V3 booster fell into the Gulf of Mexico, where it was later recovered
fullText:
SpaceX came up short on an ambitious double-catch attempt during Friday’s Launch 15, snagging only one of the two rockets it aimed to recover. The company hoped to capture both the Starship spacecraft and the Super Heavy V3 booster, building on a maneuver it first pulled off with a single booster just over two years ago and has since repeated multiple times.

		

			

SpaceX’s Launch 15 lifted off cleanly Friday evening, reaching orbit to deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites before the stages returned to Earth. Back in Boca Chica, Texas, ground crews aimed to snag the upgraded Super Heavy V3 booster using Mechazilla, SpaceX’s towering launch-and-catch structure. While the company had previously caught its older V1 booster three times, Friday’s flight marked its first attempt to recover the V3 variant.

That recovery attempt fell short. SpaceX is still investigating the cause, though spokesperson Kate Tice noted during Friday’s webcast that the booster “ended its boostback (burn) early due to a low fuel mass alarm.” The premature shutdown forced the Super Heavy V3 to splash down in the Gulf of Mexico, where recovery crews later retrieved it.

Meanwhile, the upper-stage Starship pressed on, deploying its satellites and completing roughly 14 orbits before reentering on Saturday. Nearly 24 hours after liftoff, SpaceX successfully caught the returning spacecraft with Mechazilla.

		

			

“Starship navigated its way back to the east coast of Texas, flew a final swoosh maneuver out over the Gulf, and approached the same launch site it had just left 22.5 hours prior,” SpaceX said in a statement. “After breaking through the clouds, three Raptor engines ignited for a landing flip and slow descent into Mechazilla’s waiting arms, which closed to catch Starship for the very first time.”

The initial goal was to catch both the Super Heavy V3 booster and the Starship itself, a feat that SpaceX had not attempted before. It also would’ve been the first time in human history that a space company caught both its booster rocket and the upper stage, which would’ve scored a big win for rocket reusability. 

How to watch Flight 15

SpaceX streamed the flight from its X account and the company’s website. You can watch the entire webcast on X. It lasts approximately 23.5 hours and covers the launch, the Super Heavy V3 crash into the Gulf of Mexico and the eventual catch of the Starship.

title: Here’s one small change that could improve iPhone Duo’s unoptimized apps
snippet: iPhone Duo has been out for about 3 weeks now, and I’ve happily been using mine since launch day. Many people have made a big deal about the app situation, but I’d largely say most apps I rely on are updated for iOS 27.0 at least. That said, a fair number of apps are still from iOS 26 and earlier, and those apps have letterboxing. In my time since trying the phone, I feel one quick adjustment could make the letterboxing a lot less of an issue. more…
fullText:
iPhone Duo has been out for about 3 weeks now, and I’ve happily been using mine since launch day. Many people have made a big deal about the app situation, but I’d largely say most apps I rely on are updated for iOS 27.0 at least.

That said, a fair number of apps are still from iOS 26 and earlier, and those apps have letterboxing. In my time since trying the phone, I feel one quick adjustment could make the letterboxing a lot less of an issue.

Right now, on the home screen, iPhone Duo allows you to long press an app and open it in Split View. All iPhone Duo apps allow Split View, even if the developer hasn’t compiled it for iOS 27 or 27.1.

One of the beautiful things about iPhone Duo Split View is the fact that you don’t have to decide what you’re splitting right away. On the other half of the display, you’ll see your home screen, and you can later decide what app to open.

iPhone Duo apps should have a default ‘open in split view’ option

So, given the fact that a non iOS 27 app will only occupy around half of the inner display anyways, I feel like it’d make sense to have an option to open every non-optimized app in Split View by default – rather than needing to select it every time. Or, better yet, toggle certain apps to always open in Split View.

Certain apps, even if they’re optimized for iOS 27, don’t quite feel right spread across the wider inner display of iPhone Duo – so it’d be nice to always have them in a half split without needing to think about it.

This would be a small UX improvement that I feel would go a long way, so if Apple could implement this on iPhone Duo – it’d certainly help out the app situation. While they’re at it, it’d be nice to have Slide Over on the iPhone Duo, for when you want to quickly see a smaller app on top of your full screen app.

title: Apple engineers ‘actively working’ on Face ID for iPhone Duo 2’s outer display: report
snippet: Next fall, Apple will introduce its second-generation iPhone Duo. It’s unclear what it’ll offer in terms of meaningful upgrades outside of the usual chip upgrades and camera improvements, but Apple engineers are reportedly attempting to bake Face ID into the device. That said, the feature might not make the cutoff. more…
fullText:
Next fall, Apple will introduce its second-generation iPhone Duo. It’s unclear what it’ll offer in terms of meaningful upgrades outside of the usual chip upgrades and camera improvements, but Apple engineers are reportedly attempting to bake Face ID into the device. That said, the feature might not make the cutoff.

According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple has two priorities for iPhone Duo: Face ID and the Action Button. The latter might just end up being a new software addition to Camera Control that allows you to remap the hold action from Siri in Camera to an app of your choice. 

As for Face ID, Apple engineers are ‘actively working’ on integrating the technology on the device, specifically on the outer display:

Other goals for the next couple of generations include adding a telephoto camera and making the device thinner and lighter overall. But Face ID is the top priority. I’m told that Apple has already developed prototypes of the iPhone Duo 2 with Face ID, and engineers are still actively working to integrate the facial-recognition system into the outer display of the second-generation model.

That said, the feature might not make it. According to Gurman, the timelines are tight here and it isn’t quite ready – so he isn’t reporting with certainty on whether or not this feature will make it. If it doesn’t debut with the iPhone Duo 2, it’ll likely be in the cards for iPhone Duo 3 in 2028.

Later down the road, the company wants to introduce an improved camera system for the iPhone Duo, including a telephoto camera. It also wants to make the device even thinner and lighter. The Duo definitely needs to be lighter, but making it even thinner would be an interesting feat.

9to5Mac’s Take

While Face ID on the iPhone Duo would certainly be much appreciated, I’m not quite convinced that it’ll be super meaningful on only the outer display. 

	

I’m fine with Touch ID, but whenever it is bothersome, it’s usually on the inner display, where it can be hard to reach the button depending on how you’re holding the device. If I could only have Face ID on one display, I think I’d rather have it on the inner display. 

Orientation can make a huge difference for how you reach Touch ID on the inner display, whereas you’re generally only going to hold the outer display one of two ways: upright in your left hand, or upright in your right hand.

title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Is Almost Out. Here’s How to Make Room on Your Console
snippet: You don’t have to delete old games to make space for GTA 6 if you don’t want to. Here are your other options.
fullText:
The wait is almost over. Grand Theft Auto 6 hits shelves tomorrow, Nov. 19, and if you preordered the game, you can preload it on your PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X/S now. Preloading ensures you can quickly boot the game up when it’s released.

Rockstar Games revealed that GTA 6 is 212 GB, which will take up about half of my Xbox Series S’s storage space. The company announced that GTA 6 is available to stream via Xbox Cloud Gaming without downloading it to your console. However, cloud streaming GTA 6 might affect the game’s performance and relies heavily on a strong internet connection. To avoid those issues, I plan on downloading the game.

If you’re like me and are excited to play GTA 6 but don’t have much storage space, you have two options: delete games or upgrade your console’s hard drive. Here’s what you should know about both options.

			

More from CNET

Deleting files is the easiest and cheapest way to make room for GTA 6

Rockstar Games

The simplest and cheapest way to free up space on your console for Grand Theft Auto 6 is to delete files and other games, which is what I’ll be doing. Uninstalling games is a good choice for folks who plan on spending a lot of time with GTA 6 and don’t intend to juggle different games. Rob Nelson, who oversees Rockstar North with Aaron Garbut, told The New York Times that he had an 80-hour playthrough of the game in February, so you can easily stay immersed in Grand Theft Auto’s state of Leonida.

You may not need to delete much – uninstalling a game like Call of Duty alone could free up nearly 315 GB, giving you enough digital storage for GTA 6. Since deleting files is almost instantaneous, you can quickly reclaim hard drive space. Because you don’t need to buy additional storage, you’ll also save a lot of money – storage prices are through the roof at the moment.

Deleting games doesn’t mean you’ll lose your save files, trophies or achievements. Simply reinstall a game on your console to continue playing, although even that may be unnecessary with a game streaming plan. If you’re an Xbox Game Pass or PlayStation Plus Premium subscriber, you can stream some games to your console without downloading them. 

Ultimately, deleting games is a great option if you don’t want to spend any additional money or you don’t mind redownloading games later.

Upgrading your console’s storage space lets you jump between GTA 6 and other titles

Rockstar Games

If you plan on hopping between GTA 6 and other games, or you don’t want to delete many of your downloaded titles, you can upgrade your console’s storage. Buying storage is more expensive than deleting files from your console, but benefit from being able to seamlessly hop between Grand Theft Auto 6 and Call of Duty or Madden.

You can use internal or external storage for your console, but you might have to move files between your internal and external storage to launch games. An internal hard drive lets you seamlessly play games. Xbox consoles rely on proprietary expansion cards from Seagate or SanDisk that plug into your console for additional storage. The PlayStation 5 uses M.2 solid-state drives, which are installed alongside the PS5’s built-in storage, and CNET’s David Carnoy recommends the Lexar NM 790 as a fast SSD with a straightforward installation process.

There shouldn’t be any performance, quality or load-time differences between running games from installed storage expansion devices versus your console’s internal storage. Both expansion cards and SSDs can be expensive, especially when compared with deleting games. 

External hard drives work, but you can’t launch all games from them

Rockstar Games

You could also use an external hard drive to expand your storage, which can be cheaper than buying expansion cards and internal SSD upgrades – you may even have a compatible USB external drive sitting around that you can use. However, there are caveats around what games can and can’t be played directly from external HDDs.

For Xbox consoles, some older Xbox, Xbox 360 and Xbox One titles can be stored and played from external HDDs. But games optimized for Series X/S consoles can only be stored on HDDs and must be moved back to your internal drive to play. Similarly, the PlayStation 5 only lets you store PS5 games on external HDDs, while you can store and run PS4 games from external drives. 

Therefore, using an external HDD requires playing digital musical chairs, moving current-gen games back and forth between your external hard drive and internal console storage in order to play them. The LaCie Rugged SSD4 earned a CNET Editors’ Choice Award and could be a good option. If its price tag scares you, the Western Digital P10 offers more storage at a more economical price point.

Xbox users may not need to install Grand Theft Auto 6

Rockstar Games

Rockstar announced that GTA 6 will be available to stream on the Xbox consoles – no download required – via Xbox Cloud Gaming, with some quality and time limitations. You’ll need to purchase either an Xbox Game Pass plan or Cloud Gaming hours. Folks who don’t want to delete games or upgrade their console storage can stream GTA 6, but you’ll need an Xbox One or Series X/S console, won’t get the highest visual quality and will have to pay for more playtime hours if they run out. Streaming GTA 6 could help budget-conscious gamers who don’t want to upgrade from Xbox One consoles or who don’t have the allotted storage space on their devices.

Normally, you can stream many games on PCs, mobile devices and TVs or streaming devices using Xbox Cloud Gaming or Game Pass, but Grand Theft Auto 6 is limited to the Xbox One, Series S and Series X. Additionally, GTA 6 streaming quality is capped at Series S graphical settings. So if you have a Series X, consider deleting games or upgrading your storage to run the game locally with better graphics. 

Xbox Cloud Gaming time restrictions further tamp down how much you can play. Existing Game Pass subscribers in select markets were grandfathered into unlimited Cloud Gaming so long as they keep auto-renewal enabled and maintain an active subscription. But outside of certain regions, Game Pass and Cloud Gaming subscribers face limitations on streaming hours, with the top-tier Game Pass Ultimate subscription providing 15 hours of monthly cloud gaming. You can purchase additional hours, and for GTA 6, you’ll likely blow through your allowance quickly.

While you’ll need to install the full game on your console first, remote play for Xbox and PlayStation consoles lets you stream GTA 6 to other devices, like your phone, tablet, streaming device or TV.

You can make room for GTA 6 by deleting games, buying more storage or streaming it

Rockstar Games

If you’re willing to pay a little more for the convenience of having multiple games ready to play at a moment’s notice, Xbox expansion cards or an internal SSD for a PS5 are your best options. If you want a cheaper option and don’t mind moving game files around, an external hard drive could be for you. If you have Xbox Game Pass or Xbox Cloud Gaming, you could stream the game to your console without needing more storage space. However, the cheapest option is to delete games from your internal storage and redownload them later, which can be time-consuming. 

You only have a few days left until Rockstar releases GTA 6, so you’d better prepare your digital storage now, or you might not be immediately able to play. I plan on deleting old games to make room on my console. You won’t catch me slipping on Nov. 19.

The wait is almost over. Grand Theft Auto 6 hits shelves tomorrow, Nov. 19, and if you preordered the game, you can preload it on your PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X/S now. Preloading ensures you can quickly boot the game up when it’s released.

Rockstar Games revealed that GTA 6 is 212 GB, which will take up about half of my Xbox Series S’s storage space. The company announced that GTA 6 is available to stream via Xbox Cloud Gaming without downloading it to your console. However, cloud streaming GTA 6 might affect the game’s performance and relies heavily on a strong internet connection. To avoid those issues, I plan on downloading the game.

title: Pebblebee’s latest Android Find Hub trackers try some festive colors, but fall short on sparkle
snippet: Available now, Pebblebee’s latest Android Find Hub tracker color drop might also be the first real miss, with the festive theme falling short of what it’s supposed to look like. more…
fullText:
Available now, Pebblebee’s latest Android Find Hub tracker color drop might also be the first real miss, with the festive theme falling short of what it’s supposed to look like.

Pebblebee has been dropping limited-time color variants of its Clip 5 tracker for Android Find Hub and Apple Find My all year, with the latest release this week including “Cranberry” and “Champagne.”

The new drop looks nice in marketing photos, but I will say, this is the first time I’ve felt the colors have missed the mark in person. “Cranberry” is a nice red color, but the bits of reflective sparkle shown in Pebblebee’s images don’t translate very well into real life. “Champagne” takes that a step further, with a very muted beige color that doesn’t have the shine seen in some of the listing photos.

They still look nice enough, just know you’re not getting the flashy, festive colors.

	

The good news, though, is that you’re still getting the same core hardware. USB-C rechargeable battery, support for Android Find Hub and Apple Find My, 130dB siren, and more, all for the usual $34.99. 

Pebblebee Clip 5 on Amazon

The “little extra sparkle” doesn’t translate to real life, unfortunately

The previous “Hotline Pink” and “Techno Lime” are still available for a limited time, and Pebblebee’s website has a Black Friday sale live, offering 20-30% off when you buy multiple trackers and use the code “BFCM26” at checkout.

App Store editorial team selects 45 apps and games as 2026 award finalists

If you’re up for trying out a new app or game, today Apple has highlighted 45 that are well worth your attention.

The App Store editorial team has selected 45 games and apps that are finalists for its 2026 App Store Awards. They span Apple’s various platforms, with dedicated finalists for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, and watchOS. Here are the iPhone finalists:

iPhone App and Game of the Year Finalists

ElevenReader, for reading aloud text in surprisingly natural-sounding AI voices.

(Not Boring) Camera, for transforming iPhone into a customizable old-school camera.

Raylie, for offering a personalized, guided journey for every flight.

BALL x PIT, for breaking the mold of brick breakers.

DAVE THE DIVER, for exploring the oceans deep.

Apple has also highlighted a variety of apps and games for their cultural impact.

Cultural Impact App and Game of the Year Finalists

Brilliant, for teaching the foundations of math and science.

chilli, for making it easy to take political action for the planet.

Hearing Buddy, for helping people who are deaf or hard of hearing follow the conversation.

Karrot, for enabling circular economies among neighbors.

setlog, for bringing more authenticity to social media.

and Roger, for telling a poignant and often challenging personal story.

snippet: Good morning. fullText:
Good morning. Today I’m finding open source alternatives to all of my apps, poring through Pitchfork’s list of the 100 best indie rock albums to find ones I haven’t listened to, and preparing my body for November 19th by pre-loading GTA VI (and replaying GTA IV in the meantime). 

Inbox is the tech newsletter that goes beyond the news cycle. We cover the most important 9to5Google stories from the last couple of days along with a few highlights from around the web. We publish every Tuesday and Thursday, and if you like what you read, please subscribe.

Inbox is written by Daniel Bader. Read previous issues here, and then catch up with Ben Schoon’s excellent Weekender column published every Sunday.

⭐️ Starred

On Monday, I unboxed the iPhone Duo I pre-ordered back in October and experienced a disarming sense of déjà vu. It’s beautiful hardware married to a messy, often painful software onboarding experience atypical of Apple’s usual polish. It reminds me of the Galaxy Fold’s early years.

I was most looking forward to the combination of a foldable form factor and Apple’s superior app ecosystem, but even the apps that have been updated to support the new aspect ratio, on both the front and back, feel ungainly and buggy. In moving UI elements from the bottom to the right, even with the display open, the Duo forces a rebuilding of essential muscle memory that’s prevailed across mobile platforms, including Android foldables, for 20 years.

The front display, in particular, is a massive test of one’s patience: apps, even ones ostensibly optimized for its stout dimensions, often feel unusable, with UI elements that would be prominent on the iPhone 18 Pro hidden behind overflow menus on the Duo. It’s exasperating and, frankly, boggling.

But what’s interesting is the enthusiasm with which developers are approaching the new form factor. Reddit threads reveal dozens of Duo-optimized app recommendations that feel novel and, if not polished, then propulsive. There’s a fascinating delta between waiting for my bank, or Starbucks, or Kobo, to get its act together to support the Duo and seeking out net-new opportunities and experiences.

I spent most of the summer using the Galaxy Z Fold 8, and I didn’t expect going back to it to feel so stately and predictable: the showcase of a platform with fewer highs but none of the Duo’s current lows.

I’m not sure if I’m going to keep the Duo and wait out its colicky infancy. But I do know that until now I hadn’t given Samsung enough credit for the amount of work it did to make foldable software feel ordinary, and that’s the highest compliment I can pay.

✉️ Inbox

Amazon’s new Ring cameras are mounted to roving robots, including $250 Drone Cam. If you listened to The Sideload, you’ll know I’m pretty bullish on indoor security drones and have been for some time. I don’t love that this one is from Ring, though.

The Sideload 051: Would you let Ring fly around your house?

Galaxy S27 redesign leak shows off Pro vs Ultra size difference, with just a bit of controversy. A smaller Ultra? I’m here for it.

Google and Adobe partner to add app integration in Google Drive, Gemini. Google Drive will soon work better with PDFs? Music to my freaking ears.

Gemini 4 Carbon rolling out to Gemini app for AI Ultra, Argon remains. Two weeks after the announcement, Carbon is now available, but once again it’s gated to folks who spend $100/month on tokens.

One UI 9.5 might bring Pixel 11’s ‘Rambler’ feature to Samsung Keyboard before Google’s. The Pixel 11’s best feature is coming to Samsung phones, but only through its otherwise-terrible keyboard.

Google Pixel Tag Initial Review: The gold standard for Find Hub trackers, whatever that’s worth

Pixel Tag tidbits: Surprise NFC, Find Hub setup, & Bellroy keychain cases

You can now buy the Pixel Tag, cases from Bellroy & Spigen available 

How to replace the battery on Pixel Tag [Video]

Google Pixel Tag is only available in 8 countries, and excludes Europe

Google Fi brings back network switching with ‘secondary’ partner, expands W+ beyond Pixel. Fi has always been the pricey MVNO, but I appreciate Google’s approach of backing up the cost with useful, often exclusive, features.

Google rolling out Android 17 QPR2 for Pixel. This is a big update, primarily for the Pixel 10, but everyone gets a little bit of something in November’s Pixel Drop.

November 2026 Pixel Drop: Create My Widget, HiLight for Google Messages, Pixel 10 Rambler, & more

November Pixel Watch Drop: Create My Widget, Phone-to-Watch Unlock, and Wear OS 7.1

Android 17 QPR2 November update rolling out with 33 Pixel fixes

Android Auto is getting a Gemini upgrade, but only if you use a Pixel. Will this make Android Auto more or less distracting? I can’t really tell yet.

Google rolling out Gemini app for CarPlay

Dbrand’s new Fitbit Air band launches as the first official third-party strap. I think this thing is so ugly, but I’m glad it exists as a sort of goth fitness accessory.

Motorola MA2 wireless Android Auto adapter is now available, but at nearly twice the price. Oof, a 75% price hike in six months is pretty gnarly, even in the world of RAMageddon.

You can now play Henry Cavill’s ‘Mustache Protocol’ game made on Googlebook. Please, Henry Cavill has to eat. Play his mustache game.

Google Voice appears to finally be working on RCS support. I am shocked that Google Voice still exists, frankly.

Google Wallet rolling out digital Google Home keys with supported locks on Android. This is huge news! I’ve been waiting for this announcement all year, and I can finally grab the Aqara U400 sitting in my cart.

Google Home update fixes Nest ‘Live View’ issues, improves Nest Hub and Gemini for speakers

➡️ FWD:

This section has some of our favorite stuff from around the internet. Great videos, weird memes, fun reads, recommended apps, whatever. Send us your recommendations!

Andrew’s look at the Boox Picco is a nice reminder that a gadget can be interesting because it does less. The $109 e-reader has a 4-inch screen, physical page-turn buttons, and an included magnetic case that can attach to a compatible phone. It competes directly with XTEINK’s excellent X4 Pro, which features a rudimentary touchscreen and backlight for around $100, though its magnets are built in.

Both products are wonderful examples of hardware companies adapting to the growing size and complexity of smartphones and seeing an opening for single-purpose products that do one thing really well. Plus, it’s fun to stick a thing to the back of your phone and… read it.

For something you can explore without buying another device, Paolo Mainardi turned his personal website into a point-and-click adventure. Articles live in books, links sit on a notice board, and his about page is a letter in a lighthouse. The Context Island is an incredibly thoughtful and unique approach to “web” design, and it’s another example of how AI can really help bring crazy ideas to fruition.

🗑️ Trash

We’ll likely find out today whether Jensen Huang will be removed as Nvidia’s CEO. According to the WSJ, the company’s board is preparing to oust the company’s singular chief executive, who co-founded it in 1993.

Momentum picked up after the New York Times reported that in addition to his three-year affair with Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy, Jensen had a relationship with one of his direct reports, who still works at the company.

Yikes.

Thanks for reading, and have a great day. I’ll talk to you on Tuesday.

title: Pixel Tag is a brilliant Band-Aid on a Find Hub network Google can’t easily fix
snippet: The Google Pixel Tag is here and, at least so far, it’s really good. But fresh hardware and some new features can’t fix the core problem. Google’s Find Hub network has been restricted from the very start, and it’s not something Google can easily fix. 9to5Google Weekender by Ben Schoon is a part of our free newsletter that also includes ‘Inbox,’ a twice-weekly roundup of key stories from around the web by Daniel Bader.
